サイン.etymology: Borrowed from English *sign* ('mark, symbol, signal, signboard'), from Old French *signe* and Latin *signum*. In Japanese usage it also commonly means a handwritten 'signature' or 'autograph'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — サイン

サンルーム.etymology: Borrowed from English *sunroom* ('glass-enclosed porch or room admitting abundant sunlight', from *sun* + *room*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — サンルーム

サービス.etymology: Borrowed from English *service* ('hospitality, assistance to customers'), from Old French *servise* and Latin *servitium*. In Japanese commercial usage it also developed the sense 'complimentary item, free extra, discount'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — サービス

シェフ.etymology: Borrowed from French chef (short for chef de cuisine, 'head of the kitchen').
シェフ.notes: Used both as a standalone noun and as a warm respectful title after a baker's or cook's name.

シナモン.etymology: Borrowed from English *cinnamon* ('aromatic inner bark of *Cinnamomum* trees used as a spice'), ultimately via Old French, Latin, and Greek κιννάμωμον (*kinnámōmon*) from a Semitic source.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シナモン

シナモンパン.etymology: Hybrid bakery compound ('cinnamon bread / cinnamon bun'), combining English loanword シナモン (*cinnamon*) + Portuguese loanword パン (from Portuguese *pão* 'bread', introduced in the 16th century).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シナモン

シナモンロール.etymology: Borrowed from English *cinnamon roll* ('spiraled sweet pastry seasoned with cinnamon and sugar', from *cinnamon* + *roll*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シナモンロール

シャッター.etymology: Borrowed from English *shutter* ('hinged or rolling window/shop-front cover; camera shutter', agent noun from *shut*).

history.meaning: rolling shop shutter; window shutter; camera shutter

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シャッター

シャツ.etymology: Borrowed in the Meiji period from English *shirts* (plural of *shirt*, reanalyzed in Japanese as a singular noun), from Old English *scyrte*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シャツ

シャワー.etymology: Borrowed from English shower (short for shower bath).

シンプル.etymology: Borrowed from English *simple* ('plain, uncomplicated, unadorned'), from Old French *simple* and Latin *simplex* ('single-fold, plain'). Used in Japanese as a *na*-adjective praising clean, uncluttered design.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シンプル

シーツ.etymology: Borrowed from English *sheets* (plural of *sheet* 'bedsheet', adopted as a singular noun in Japanese), from Old English *scīete* ('piece of linen cloth').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — シーツ

ジャム.etymology: Borrowed from English *jam* ('sweet fruit preserve boiled with sugar'), introduced into Japanese culinary vocabulary in the Meiji period.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ジャム

ジャムパン.etymology: Japanese bakery compound ('jam bun, bread roll filled with fruit jam'), first created in Tokyo in 1900 by Kimura-ya Bakery, combining English loanword ジャム (*jam*) + Portuguese loanword パン (*pão* 'bread').

history.meaning: sweet bread roll filled with fruit jam

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ジャムパン

スイッチ.etymology: Borrowed from English 'switch', a device that turns an electric current on and off; Japanese also uses it for railway points and, as スイッチする, for changing one's approach.

スクランブルエッグ.etymology: Borrowed from English *scrambled eggs* (with the plural *-s* and past-participle *-d* dropped in Japanese phonetic adaptation).

history.meaning: eggs beaten and pan-cooked while stirring

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — スクランブルエッグ
Wiktionary — スクランブルエッグ (Japanese)

スケッチ.etymology: Borrowed from English *sketch* ('rough drawing or outline'), from Dutch *schets* and Italian *schizzo* (ultimately from Latin *schedius* and Greek σχέδιος 'done offhand').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — スケッチ

スピーチ.etymology: Borrowed from English *speech* ('formal address or talk delivered to an audience'), from Old English *spǣċ*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — スピーチ

スプーン.etymology: Borrowed from English *spoon* ('utensil with a shallow bowl on a handle'), from Old English *spōn* ('chip or sliver of wood').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — スプーン

スポンジ.etymology: Borrowed from English sponge, ultimately from Ancient Greek σπογγιά (spongiá).
スポンジ.notes: Used both for kitchen/window sponges and sponge cake (スポンジケーキ).

スーツケース.etymology: Borrowed from English suitcase ('flat-sided Rectangular travel bag'), combining スーツ ('suit') and ケース ('case').

スープ.etymology: Borrowed from English *soup* (and French *soupe*), referring mainly to Western-style or Chinese-style soups in contrast to traditional Japanese 汁 (しる / みそ汁).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — スープ

セット.etymology: Borrowed from English *set* ('matched group of items; setting up equipment or hair; fixed-menu combination').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — セット

セリフ.etymology: Native Edo-period theatrical noun 台詞・科白 (せりふ 'actor's spoken lines on stage, remark'), derived from 競り言ふ (*seri-iu* 'speaking in turn / vying in speech') or 世流布 (*serufu*). Often written in katakana セリフ in modern prose.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 台詞

センチ.etymology: Clipped loanword from French *centimètre* / English *centimeter* (センチメートル 'centimeter, one-hundredth of a meter', from Latin *centum* 'hundred' + *mètre*). Also used as a clipping of センチメンタル (*sentimental*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — センチ

セーター.etymology: Borrowed from English *sweater* ('knitted pullover garment', originally athletic wear designed to induce sweating, from *sweat* + *-er*), with simplification of the *sw-* cluster to *s-* in Japanese.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — セーター

ゼロ.etymology: Borrowed from French *zéro* / English *zero* ('the number 0, nothing'), ultimately via Italian *zero* and Medieval Latin *zephirum* from Arabic صِفْر (*ṣifr* 'empty, zero').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ゼロ

タイマー.etymology: Borrowed from English *timer* ('device that measures elapsed time and signals when a set interval ends', agent noun from *time*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — タイマー

タイヤ.etymology: Borrowed from English *tire* / *tyre* ('rubber covering placed around a wheel rim').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — タイヤ

タオル.etymology: Borrowed in the Meiji period from English *towel* ('absorbent cloth for drying'), from Old French *toaille*. Primarily denotes Western-style looped cotton terrycloth towels in contrast to flat woven 手拭い (*tenugui*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — タオル

タクシー.etymology: Borrowed in the Taishō era from English taxi, itself clipped from taximeter cab.

タブレット.etymology: Borrowed from English *tablet* ('flat portable touchscreen computer; compressed medicinal pill or lozenge'), from Old French *tablete* ('small table or writing slate').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — タブレット

タルト.etymology: Borrowed from French *tarte* (and English *tart*), referring to a baked shortcrust pastry shell filled with fruit, custard, or cream; ultimately from Old French *tarte*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — タルト

タルト生地.etymology: Hybrid baking compound タルト生地 ('tart dough, shortcrust pastry dough'), combining French loanword タルト (*tarte*) + native/Sino-Japanese 生地 (きじ 'unworked material, dough, fabric', from 生 *ki* 'raw, natural' + 地 *ji* 'ground, base material').

history.meaning: pastry dough for a tart shell

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 生地

チェックイン.etymology: Borrowed from English *check-in* / *check in* ('registering one's arrival at a hotel, inn, or airport').

history.meaning: registration upon arrival at a hotel or airport

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — チェックイン

チョーク.etymology: Borrowed from English *chalk* ('soft white limestone or calcium sulfate stick used for writing on blackboards'), from Old English *cealc* and Latin *calx* ('lime').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — チョーク
Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ティーカップ

テーブル.etymology: Borrowed from English table to name a raised dining or café table used with chairs, in contrast with low floor tables.

history.meaning: cloth spread over a dining or café table

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — テーブルクロス

テープ.etymology: Borrowed from English *tape* ('narrow strip of adhesive cloth/plastic, ribbon, or magnetic recording strip'), from Old English *tæppe* ('strip of cloth').

history.meaning: adhesive strip, ribbon, or recording tape

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — テープ

デシベル.etymology: Borrowed from English *decibel* (and French *décibel*), the logarithmic unit of sound intensity combining metric prefix *deci-* ('one-tenth', from Latin *decimus*) + *bel* (named in honor of telephone pioneer Alexander Graham Bell).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — デシベル

トマト.etymology: Borrowed from English *tomato*, which came via Spanish *tomate* from Nahuatl *tomatl* ('swelling fruit'). Introduced to Japan as an ornamental plant in the Edo period (called 赤茄子 *akanasu*) and popularized as a food crop under the name トマト in the Meiji–Taishō era.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — トマト

トラック.etymology: Borrowed from two converging English words: (1) American English *truck* ('motor vehicle for hauling freight'), and (2) English *track* ('running track, path, or recorded audio track').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — トラック

トレイ.etymology: Borrowed from English tray, tracing back to Old English trīg ('wooden board or shallow dish').
トレイ.notes: Also spelled トレー; standard word in cafés and bakeries for baking and serving trays.

トースト.etymology: Borrowed from English *toast* ('sliced bread browned by radiant heat'), from Old French *toster* ('to roast, grill') and Latin *tostus* ('parched, roasted').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — トースト

ト長調.etymology: Meiji-era Japanese musical terminology ('G major'), combining ト (the 7th symbol of the traditional *iroha* syllabary, assigned in Japanese music theory to the 5th scale degree / pitch G, equivalent to Western A–B–C–D–E–F–G mapped to イ–ロ–ハ–ニ–ホ–ヘ–ト) + Sino-Japanese 長調 (ちょうちょう 'major key', from 長 'major/long' + 調 'key, mode').

history.form: ト (iroha note G) + 長調 (major key)
ト長調 (とちょうちょう)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ト長調
Wiktionary — ト長調 (とちょうちょう) (Japanese)

ド.etymology: Borrowed from Italian solfège syllable *do* ('the first note of the diatonic scale, C in fixed-do'), introduced in 17th-century Italy (replacing Guido of Arezzo's *ut*) and adopted into Japanese music education in the Meiji period.

history.meaning: first degree of the scale; pitch C

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — ド

ドア.etymology: Borrowed from English door, referring specifically to a hinged or automatic Western-style door rather than a sliding Japanese 戸 (to) or 襖 (fusuma).

ドキドキ.etymology: Katakana orthographic spelling of the reduplicated mimetic word どきどき, imitating the rapid thumping or pounding of the heart from excitement, suspense, or nervousness.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — どきどき

バケツ.etymology: Borrowed from English bucket (reflecting English plural buckets or palatalized final -t -> -tsu).
バケツ.notes: Replaced wooden pails (桶 おけ) for everyday metal and plastic household buckets.

バター.etymology: Borrowed in the Meiji period from English butter as Western dairy and baking spread across Japan.

パイプ.etymology: Borrowed from English pipe for both plumbing/heating tubes and smoking pipes.

パン.etymology: Borrowed in the sixteenth century from Portuguese pão ('bread'), introduced by Portuguese traders and missionaries in Nagasaki and remaining one of Japanese's oldest everyday European loanwords.

ビスケット.etymology: Borrowed from English biscuit (compare 16th-century Portuguese loan ビスカウト), ultimately from Latin bis coctus ('twice baked').
ビスケット.notes: Refers to crisp tea biscuits baked to hold well beside hot tea or coffee.

ピアノ.etymology: Borrowed via English and Italian piano (short for Italian pianoforte, 'soft-loud').

ピンセット.etymology: Borrowed in the late Edo / early Meiji period from Dutch pincet ('tweezers'), itself from French pincette (diminutive of pince, 'pincers').
ピンセット.notes: Entered Japanese through Dutch medical and scientific studies (蘭学) and remains the everyday word for precision tweezers.

フェルト.etymology: Borrowed from English felt, denoting non-woven cloth matted together from wool fibres by heat and moisture.
フェルト.notes: Essential inside upright and grand pianos for hammers, dampers, and action bushings.

フロント.etymology: Japanese hospitality clipping (和製英語 shortening) from English front desk / front office.
フロント.notes: Standard word at both Western hotels and modernised ryokan for the reception counter.

ペダル.etymology: Borrowed from English pedal, ultimately from Latin pedālis ('of the foot', from pēs, pedis 'foot').
ペダル.notes: Used for upright and grand piano foot pedals as well as bicycle pedals.

ホテル.etymology: Borrowed in the Meiji era from English hotel (ultimately from French hôtel) to distinguish Western-style hotels from traditional Japanese inns (旅館).

ポケット.etymology: Borrowed from English pocket with Western tailored clothing in the Meiji era.

ミルク.etymology: Borrowed from English milk; in everyday Japanese ミルク often refers to milk added to coffee or tea, alongside Sino-Japanese 牛乳 for fresh drinking milk.

メートル.etymology: Borrowed from French mètre, the metric unit of length. Japanese also has the doublet メーター, from English 'meter', which now usually means a measuring instrument; the old kanji spellings were 米 and 米突.

ラベル.etymology: Borrowed via Dutch label / early English spelling pronunciation, rather than later English /ˈleɪbəl/ (which separately gave レーベル for record labels).
ラベル.notes: Everyday Japanese distinguishes ラベル (paper jar or bottle label) from レーベル (music/publishing imprint).

ランプ.etymology: Borrowed from Dutch lamp and English lamp in the nineteenth century, initially for oil and kerosene lamps and later for electric desk and reading lamps.

レンズ豆.etymology: Partial calque combining English/German loan レンズ ('lens', ultimately from Latin lēns, 'lentil') with native 豆 (まめ, 'bean, pulse').
レンズ豆.notes: Optics borrowed Latin lēns ('lentil') for glass lenses because of their curved lentil shape, and Japanese named the legume 'lens-bean' in turn!

一言一句.etymology: Four-character Sino-Japanese idiom (四字熟語) 一言一句 (いちごんいっく), pairing 一言 ('a single word') and 一句 ('a single phrase').
一言一句.notes: Uses traditional go'on reading ごん for 言 in set classical expressions.

中庭.etymology: Native Japanese compound (jukujikun/kun-reading) of 中 ('inside, inner') and 庭 ('garden, courtyard'), naming an enclosed courtyard surrounded by wings or walls of a house or inn.

予約.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 予 ('beforehand, in advance') and 約 ('promise, agreement'), meaning an advance booking or reservation.

作曲家.etymology: Three-character Sino-Japanese compound 作曲家 (さっきょくか): 作 ('make, create') + 曲 ('melody, piece of music') + specialist suffix -家 ('master, professional').
作曲家.notes: Shares 曲 with 楽曲 and specialist suffix -家 with 建築家 ('architect').

値段.etymology: Compound of native 値 (ね, 'value, worth') and Sino-Japanese 段 (だん, 'step, grade, level'), literally 'the level of worth' of an item.

元気.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 元 ('origin, foundation') and 気 ('vital energy, breath'), originally referring to the fundamental life force of nature and people, and in everyday speech meaning 'lively, healthy, in good spirits'.

history.meaning: primordial vitality; good health and spirits

再開.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 再開 (さいかい), from 再 ('again, a second time') and 開 ('open, begin').
再開.notes: Used when an inn, shop, or concert series opens its doors again after an interruption.

写真.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 写 ('copy, depict') and 真 ('truth, the real thing'): 'copying the true likeness'. It first named painted portraits of deities and nobles; in the late Edo period it also meant drawing from life, and when photographs arrived from the West at the end of the Edo period it was adopted as the translation of English 'photograph', gradually replacing rivals such as 写真絵 and 照画.

history.meaning: portrait of a deity or noble person

sources.title: Shogakukan: Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 写真 (語誌)

切符.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 切符 (きっぷ, with gemination from きりふ), combining 切 ('cut, notch') and 符 ('tally slip, voucher').
切符.notes: Originally denoted a wooden or paper tally cut in two as proof of payment; adopted in the Meiji railway era for train and theatre tickets.

刷毛.etymology: Native Japanese noun はけ (related to 掃く はく, 'to sweep, brush across'), spelled with semantic ateji 刷毛 ('brushing-hair').
刷毛.notes: Refers to wide flat brushes used in carpentry, painting, dyeing, and pastry glazing.

割引.etymology: Compound of 割り ('tenth-part proportion, rate', from 割る 'divide') and 引き ('pulling back, subtracting', from 引く), literally 'subtracting a proportion off the price'.

半額.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 半 ('half') and 額 ('monetary amount, stated sum'), literally 'half the stated sum'.

受け皿.etymology: Native compound of 受ける ('receive, catch, support') in stem form 受け and 皿 ('plate, dish', voiced to ざら by rendaku), literally 'a dish that catches a cup above it'.

台所.etymology: Compound 台所 (だいどころ), joining 台 (だい, 'raised stand or tray table for preparing food') and 所 (ところ -> -どころ by rendaku, 'place').
台所.notes: Originated in aristocratic households for the room where meal stands (台盤) were arranged; became the universal warm home word for 'kitchen'.

名前.etymology: Native Japanese compound of 名 (*na*, 'name') and 前 (*mae*, 'front, presence, assigned portion'), originally polite or formal and now the standard everyday noun for 'name'.

和音.etymology: Sino-Japanese musical compound 和音 (わおん), from 和 ('harmony, blending together') and 音 ('musical tone').
和音.notes: Standard term for a musical chord sounded simultaneously on piano or strings.

土曜日.etymology: Compound of 土曜 ('Saturn day', associated with the Five Phases element 土 'earth') and 日 ('day'), part of the seven-day week standardized officially in Meiji-era Japan in 1876.

morphemes.meaning: celestial luminary; day of the week

土砂降り.etymology: Hybrid compound joining Sino-Japanese 土砂 (どしゃ, 'earth and gravel') with native 降り (ふり -> -ぶり via rendaku, from 降る 'fall, pour down').
土砂降り.notes: Likens a blinding cloudburst to earth and stones pouring straight out of the sky.

埋まる.etymology: Intransitive verb ('to be buried, be filled up') derived from the Old Japanese transitive verb うむ (埋む, 'to bury, fill in') with the intransitive suffix -aru.

history.meaning: bury; cover with earth; fill in
be buried; be filled (of seats, schedules, holes)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 埋まる

堂々.etymology: Sino-Japanese reduplicated adverb/tari-adjective 堂々 (dōdō), borrowed from Literary Chinese 堂堂 ('stately, imposing, grand, open and aboveboard'), reduplicating 堂 ('grand hall').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 堂々

堅苦しい.etymology: Native Japanese compound adjective formed from the stem of かたい (堅い・固い, 'hard, stiff, rigid') + くるしい (苦しい, 'painful, oppressive, stifling'), literally 'stiffly oppressive'.

history.form: 堅苦しい (かたくるしい)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 堅苦しい

場所.etymology: Compound noun combining native Japanese ば (場, 'place, spot, arena') with the noun ところ/しょ (所, 'place, site'), read with the hybrid yomi ばしょ (jūbako reading).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 場所

塗り替える.etymology: Compound verb formed from the continuative stem ぬり (塗り, from 塗る 'to paint, coat, plaster') + かえる (替える, 'to replace, redo').

history.form: 塗り替える (ぬりかえる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 塗り替える

塗る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *nuru* ('to smear, coat, plaster, paint'), attested in the Man'yōshū; likely related to ぬる (濡る, 'to get wet') and ぬるぬる ('slimy, slippery').

history.meaning: smear; daub; apply lacquer or mud

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 塗る

塩.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sifo* ('salt; seawater; tide'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, undergoing regular medial *-f- > -w- > Ø* change to modern *shio*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 塩

塩バター.etymology: Modern hybrid culinary compound combining native Japanese しお (塩, 'salt') + loanword バター (from English *butter*), referring to salted butter or salt-butter flavoring.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — バター

壁.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *kabe₁* ('mud or plaster wall, partition'), attested in the Man'yōshū and Wamyō Ruijushō.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 壁

壊す.etymology: Transitive godan verb *kowasu* ('to break, destroy, demolish'), formed as the transitive counterpart to こわれる (壊れる) from the verbal root *kowa-* ('break apart').

history.form: こぼつ / こわす (壊す)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 壊す

壊れる.etymology: Intransitive ichidan verb *kowareru* ('to break, be broken, fall apart'), continuing Late Middle Japanese lower bigrade こわる (壊る), related to classical こぼつ/こぼる ('to break down').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 壊れる

声.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ko₂we* ('voice, sound, cry'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; medial *-w-* was lost before *e* in Middle Japanese, yielding modern *koe*.

history.meaning: voice; vocal sound; cry of a bird or insect

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 声

売る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *uru* ('to sell, offer in exchange'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: sell; put on sale; make known (a name)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 売る

売却.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 売却 (baikyaku), from 売 ('sell') + 却 (originally a completive particle in Chinese vernaculary usage, 'dispose of, away'), meaning 'selling off, disposal by sale'.

history.meaning: sell off; dispose of by sale

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 売却

壺.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tubo* ('round-bellied jar, pot, deep vessel'), attested in the Nihon Shoki and Wamyō Ruijushō.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 壺

変.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and na-adjective 変 (hen), from Middle Chinese 變 (*pjiᴇnH*, 'change, transformation, unusual event, anomaly'); in Edo-period and modern Japanese used adjectivally for 'strange, odd, peculiar'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 変

変える.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *kaeru* ('to change, alter'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade かふ (変ふ・代ふ), the transitive partner of かわる (変わる).

history.meaning: exchange; alter; turn into something else

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 変える

変わる.etymology: Intransitive godan verb *kawaru* ('to change, be altered, vary'), continuing Old Japanese かはる (変はる・代はる), formed from the root *kafa-* + intransitive *-ru*.

history.meaning: undergo change; shift; take the place of
change; be transformed; vary; be unusual

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 変わる

夏.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *natu* ('summer'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; often compared internally with あつし (暑し・熱し, 'hot').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夏

夕方.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun combining ゆふ (夕, 'evening, dusk') + かた (方, 'direction, time around'), literally 'toward evening'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夕方

夕空.etymology: Native Japanese poetic and descriptive compound combining ゆう (夕, from Old Japanese *yufu*, 'evening') + そら (空, 'sky').

history.form: ゆふぞら / ゆふそら (夕空)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夕空

夕食.etymology: Compound of ゆう (夕, 'evening') + しょく (食, Sino-Japanese reading for 'meal, food'), or read purely Sino-Japanese as せきしょく; in modern standard usage read as the jūbako hybrid ゆうしょく ('evening meal, dinner').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夕食

外.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *so₂to₂* ('outside, exterior, out of doors'), likely a compound of *so* ('back, away') + *to* ('place, door').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 外

外す.etymology: Transitive godan verb *hazusu* ('to unfasten, remove, miss'), paired with intransitive はずれる (外れる, classical はづる 'to come off, miss a notch').

history.meaning: release from the bowstring notch; undo; miss
unfasten; take off; remove; miss; step away

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 外す

外側.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining そと (外, 'outside, exterior') + がわ (側, voiced from かわ 'side, row').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 外側

多い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese adjective *oposi* (多し, 'numerous, abundant, many'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; medial *-p- > -f- > -w- > Ø* yielded modern *ōi*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 多い

多め.etymology: Derived noun/na-adjective formed from the stem おお- of 多い ('many, much') + suffix -め (目, 'degree, tendency, somewhat on the ... side').

history.meaning: a generous amount; somewhat more than usual

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 多め

夜.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yo₁ru* ('night'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, extended from the shorter root *yo₁* (夜, 'night') with the temporal/locative suffix *-ru* (compare *firu* 昼).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夜

夜分.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 夜分 (yabun), from 夜 ('night') + 分 ('division, time period'), attested in Chinese and adopted into Japanese as a polite expression for 'nighttime, late in the evening'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夜分

夜明け.etymology: Native Japanese compound 夜明け (よあけ), from 夜 (よ, 'night') and 明け (あけ, nominalized stem of 明ける 'to grow light, dawn').
夜明け.notes: Evokes the transition from night darkness to first morning light.

夢.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yume₂* (earlier *ime₂*, 'dream'), attested in the Man'yōshū; widely analyzed as derived from い (寝, 'sleep') + め (目, 'eye, seeing'), literally 'sleep-vision'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 夢

大きい.etymology: Adjectival derivative formed in Late Middle Japanese from Earlier Japanese おほきなり (大きなり, from Old Japanese *opoki₁* 'big, great'), shifting from a naru-adjective to an i-adjective.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大きい

大きな.etymology: Prenominal determiner (rentaishi) shortened from 大きなる (*ōkinaru*), the adnominal form of the classical naru-adjective 大きなり ('large, great').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大きな

大丈夫.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 大丈夫 (daijōbu), originally from Classical Chinese ('a great, stalwart man of principle; a hero in full vigor'). In Japanese it shifted from 'strong, reliable person' to 'secure, sturdy, safe, all right'.

history.meaning: man of great stature and moral resolve
all right; safe; okay; no problem

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大丈夫

大事.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 大事 (daiji), from 大 ('great') + 事 ('matter, affair'). Originally 'a major event or grave crisis' in Buddhist and classical texts, whence 'something to be treated with great care, precious, important'.

history.meaning: great undertaking; matter of life and death
serious affair; emergency; something requiring care

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大事

大切.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 大切 (taisetsu), from 大 ('great') + 切 ('urgent, pressing, keen'). Originally 'urgent necessity, critical moment' in medieval Japanese, later shifting to 'valuable, important, cherished'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大切

大声.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun combining おお- (大, 'big, loud') + ごえ (声, rendaku form of こえ 'voice').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大声

大変.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 大変 (taihen), from 大 ('great, major') + 変 ('unusual event, calamity, upheaval'). From 'major disaster or serious incident', it bleached in Edo-period speech into 'dreadful, tough' and an intensifier 'very, extremely'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大変

大失敗.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound prefixing 大 (dai-, 'great, huge') to 失敗 (shippai, 'failure, blunder').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 失敗

大好き.etymology: Hybrid compound prefixing Sino-Japanese 大 (dai-, 'greatly, very much') to native Japanese すき (好き, 'liking, fondness').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大好き

大家さん.etymology: Polite title formed from おおや (大家 / 大屋, 'main house; landlord, house-owner') + honorific suffix -さん (from さま 様).

history.meaning: landlord of a tenement or rental house

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大家

大工.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 大工 (daiku), originally an official Ritsuryō court title ('master artisan, chief builder') above 小工 (shōku); by the medieval period it generalized to 'carpenter'.

history.meaning: chief master builder of state construction

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大工

大輝.etymology: Japanese masculine given name (commonly read Taiki or Daiki) composed of 大 ('great, large') + 輝 ('radiance, shine, brilliance').

history.form: 大輝 (たいき / だいき)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 輝

大通り.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun combining おお- (大, 'large, main') + どおり (通り, rendaku form of とおり 'street, avenue, thoroughfare').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大通り

大阪.etymology: Major city and prefecture in the Kansai region; formerly written 大坂 ('great slope'), attested as 小坂 (Ozaka) in ancient texts and renamed 大坂 in the late 15th century, with the character 阪 standardized in the Meiji era.

history.form: 大坂 (おほさか / おおさか)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大阪

大雨.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun combining おお- (大, 'heavy, great') + あめ (雨, 'rain'), attested since classical times.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 大雨

天井.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 天井 (tenjō), literally 'sky-well', referring originally in Chinese architecture and Japanese Buddhist temples to a coffered wooden lattice ceiling overhead, then any indoor ceiling.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 天井

天気.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 天 ('sky, heavens') and 気 ('air, breath, atmospheric vapor'), meaning atmospheric weather.

天気予報.etymology: Four-character Sino-Japanese compound 天気予報 (てんきよほう), pairing 天気 ('weather', literally 'sky energy') with 予報 ('advance report, forecast').
天気予報.notes: Coined in the Meiji meteorological service and used daily in broadcasts and conversation.

太い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *puto₁si* (太し, 'thick, stout, grand, sacredly auspicious'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: thick; fat; deep (of a voice); bold

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 太い

太っ腹.etymology: Colloquial compound formed from the geminated stem ふとっ- (from 太い 'thick, big') + はら (腹, 'belly, gut, spirit, disposition'), literally 'big-bellied' in the figurative sense of 'magnanimous, generous, big-hearted'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 太っ腹

太陽.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 太陽 (taiyō), from Classical Chinese 太陽 ('supreme yang; the sun', in contrast to 太陰 'supreme yin; the moon').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 太陽

失くす.etymology: Transitive godan verb *nakusu* ('to lose, misplace, get rid of'), formed from the adverbial stem なく of ない (無い, 'nonexistent, gone') + transitive verbalizer -す (written with 失 by semantic association with 'losing').

history.meaning: cause to disappear; do away with; lose

history.form: 失くす / 無くす (なくす)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 無くす

失礼.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 失礼 (shitsurei), from Classical Chinese 失禮 ('to fail in礼/etiquette, commit a breach of manners'); used in Japanese both for 'discourtesy, rudeness' and in polite apologies ('excuse me').

history.meaning: rudeness; breach of etiquette; excuse me

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 失礼

契約.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 契約 (keiyaku), from Classical Chinese 契約 ('binding agreement, covenant'), combining 契 ('notched tally, deed, contract') + 約 ('bind, promise').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 契約

契約課.etymology: Sino-Japanese administrative compound combining 契約 (keiyaku, 'contract') + 課 (ka, 'administrative section, division, department').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 契約

奥.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *o₂ku* ('interior, inner depths, far back'), attested in the Man'yōshū; contrasted with はし (端, 'edge') or おもて (表, 'front').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 奥

女性.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 女性 (josei), from 女 ('woman, female') + 性 ('sex, nature, gender'), used since classical times for the female sex and in modern Japanese as the standard polite noun for 'woman'.

history.form: 女性 (にょしょう / じょせい)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 女性

好き.etymology: Nominal and na-adjectival form derived from the continuative stem of the Old Japanese verb すく (好く, 'to set one's heart on, be fond of, fancy').

history.meaning: fondness; devotion to poetry, love, or art

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 好き

妙.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and na-adjective 妙 (myō), from Middle Chinese 妙 (*mjiewH*, 'wondrous, subtle, exquisite'). From Buddhist 'wondrous, beyond ordinary comprehension', it developed the colloquial sense 'strange, curious, peculiar'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 妙

始まり.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of はじまる (始まる, 'to begin, start').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 始まり

始まる.etymology: Intransitive godan verb *hajimaru* ('to begin, start'), attested from Old Japanese, derived from the root of はじめ/はじむ (始む, 'to begin') + intransitive suffix *-aru*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 始まる

始める.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *hajimeru* ('to begin, start, initiate'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade はじむ (始む), cognate with はし (端, 'tip, first edge').

history.meaning: initiate; begin; do for the first time

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 始める

姿.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sugata* ('bodily form, figure, appearance'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 姿

嬉しい.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *uresi* (嬉し, 'joyful, delightful, pleasing'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; likely built on the emotional root *ura-* (裏・心, 'inner heart').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 嬉しい

子.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ko₁* ('child, offspring, young, small thing'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 子

子ども.etymology: Orthographic variant of 子供 (*kodomo*, 'child, children'), formed from こ (子, 'child') + plural/collective suffix -ども (共, originally marking a group of subordinates or peers, later singularized).

history.form: 子ども / 子供 (こども)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 子供

子供.etymology: Compound of Old Japanese こ (子, 'child') + plural suffix -ども (共). Originally plural ('children'), it reanalyzed in Early Modern Japanese as a singular or number-neutral noun for 'child' (pluralized again as 子供たち).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 子供

字.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 字 (ji), from Middle Chinese 字 (*dziH*, 'written character, graph, courtesy name'), originally derived from 'to bear a child under a roof' > 'breed,衍生/derive characters'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 字

学校.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 学校 (gakkō), from Classical Chinese 學校 ('school, place of learning'), combining 學 ('study, learn') + 校 ('school building, examine').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 学校

孫.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mago₁* (earlier *umago₁*, 'grandchild'), attested in the Wamyō Ruijushō; often analyzed as *uma-* + *ko₁* ('child').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 孫

守る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mamo₂ru* ('to watch closely, guard, protect'), attested in the Man'yōshū, derived from ま- (目, 'eye') + もる (守る, 'to guard, keep watch').

history.meaning: watch over with the eyes; guard; protect
protect; defend; obey (a rule); keep (a promise)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 守る

安い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yasusi* (安し・易し, 'peaceful, calm, easy, free from anxiety'). In the Edo period, 'worry-free, easy to obtain' specialized when written 安い to 'inexpensive, cheap'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 安い

安全.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 安全 (anzen), from Classical Chinese 安全 ('safe and whole, free from danger'), combining 安 ('peaceful, secure') + 全 ('whole, intact').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 安全

安心.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 安 ('peaceful, settled, safe') and 心 ('heart, mind'), literally 'a settled heart'—feeling relieved and free from worry.

完了.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 完了 (kanryō), combining 完 ('complete, whole') + 了 ('finish, bring to a close').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 完了

完全.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 完全 (kanzen), from Classical Chinese 完全 ('intact, whole, without defect'), combining 完 ('whole, complete') + 全 ('entire, intact').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 完全

完成.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 完成 (kansei), from Chinese 完成 ('to bring to completion, accomplish'), combining 完 ('complete') + 成 ('accomplish, form').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 完成

完璧.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 完璧 (kanpeki), from a Classical Chinese historical idiom in the *Shiji* (Records of the Grand Historian) in which Lin Xiangru returned the priceless He氏 jade disc (璧) intact (完) to the state of Zhao; hence 'flawless, utterly complete'.

history.meaning: return the jade disc whole and unblemished

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 完璧

定規.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 定規 (じょうぎ), from 定 ('fix, establish') and 規 ('compass, standard rule').
定規.notes: Originally denoted carpenter's measuring standards before becoming the everyday word for a straightedge ruler.

宝物.etymology: Native Japanese compound *takaramono* combining たから (宝, 'treasure', from Old Japanese *takara*) + もの (物, 'thing, object').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 宝物

実は.etymology: Discourse adverbial/conjunctive phrase formed from Sino-Japanese じつ (実, 'truth, reality') + topic particle は ('as for the truth -> in fact, to tell the truth').

history.meaning: in truth; as a matter of fact
actually; in fact; to tell the truth

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 実は

客.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 客 (kyaku / kaku), from Middle Chinese 客 (*kʰæk*, 'guest, visitor, traveler, customer').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 客

客室.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 客室 (kyakushitsu), combining 客 ('guest, passenger') + 室 ('room, chamber').

history.meaning: drawing room for guests; guest chamber
guest room (in a hotel); passenger cabin

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 客室

室内.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 室内 (shitsunai), from Classical Chinese 室内 ('inside a room, indoors'), combining 室 ('room') + 内 ('inside, interior').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 室内

家.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ipe₁* ('house, dwelling, household, family'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, undergoing medial *-p- > -f- > -w- > Ø* to modern *ie*; also read *ya* from Old Japanese *ya* ('roof, house').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 家

家具.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 家具 (kagu), from Chinese 家具 ('household utensils and furniture'), combining 家 ('house, home') + 具 ('implement, furnishing').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 家具

家族.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 家族 (kazoku), from Chinese 家族 ('household clan, family'), combining 家 ('house, household') + 族 ('clan, kin group').

history.meaning: members of a household or lineage

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 家族

家賃.etymology: Hybrid compound combining native Japanese や (家, 'house, building') + Sino-Japanese ちん (賃, 'hire, rent, fee'), attested from the Edo period for house or tenement rent.

history.meaning: fee paid for renting a house

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 家賃

宿.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yado₁* ('dwelling place, lodging for the night'), formed from *ya* (屋・家, 'house') + *to₁* (処・戸, 'place, door').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 宿

宿帳.etymology: Hybrid Japanese compound of native 宿 (やど, 'inn, lodging') and Sino-Japanese 帳 (ちょう, 'bound register book'), the traditional guest ledger kept at travellers' inns since the Edo period.

宿泊.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 宿泊 (shukuhaku), combining 宿 ('lodge for the night') + 泊 ('stop over, moor, stay overnight').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 宿泊

寂しい.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sabisi* (寂し・淋し, 'desolate, faded, lonely'), derived from the verb *sabu* ('to lose vitality, fade, grow desolate or patinated').

history.form: 寂しい (さびしい / さみしい)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 寂しい

寒い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *samusi* (寒し, 'cold, chilly' of weather or air), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; cognate with さむ (冷む, 'to cool down').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 寒い

寝る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *nu* (寝, continuative *ne-*, 'to lie down, sleep'), becoming modern ichidan *neru*.

history.meaning: sleep; go to bed; lie down

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 寝る

寸前.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 寸前 (sunzen), combining 寸 ('a Chinese inch; a tiny distance') + 前 ('before, in front of'), literally 'one inch before'.

history.meaning: right in front of one's eyes; a hair's breadth before
on the verge of; just before

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 寸前

寸法.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 寸法 (sunpō), combining 寸 ('inch, unit of length') + 法 ('method, standard, rule'), originally 'measurement standard' and by extension 'dimensions, size, plan'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 寸法

封筒.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 封筒 (fūtō), from Chinese 封筒, combining 封 ('seal, close up a letter') + 筒 ('tube, sleeve, pouch'), referring originally to a bamboo or paper tube/sleeve for sealed letters.

history.stage: Late Imperial Chinese / Early Modern Japanese

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 封筒

専用.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 専用 (sen'yō), from Classical Chinese 專用 ('use exclusively, sole use'), combining 專 ('sole, exclusive, focused') + 用 ('use, employ').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 専用

専用オフィス.etymology: Modern hybrid compound combining Sino-Japanese 専用 (sen'yō, 'exclusive/private use') + loanword オフィス (from English *office*).

history.form: 専用オフィス (せんようオフィス)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 専用

専門.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 専門 (senmon), from Classical Chinese 專門 ('devoting oneself exclusively to one school of learning or gate of scholarship'), combining 專 ('exclusive') + 門 ('gate, school, field').

history.meaning: single-minded study of one scholarly tradition

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 専門

尊敬.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 尊敬 (sonkei), from Classical Chinese 尊敬 ('to honor and revere'), combining 尊 ('revere, noble') + 敬 ('respect, hold in awe').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 尊敬

導く.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mitibiku* (導く, 'to guide along the way, lead'), a transparent compound of みち (道, 'road, way') + ひく (引く, 'to pull, lead by the hand').

history.meaning: lead by the hand along a path; guide

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 導く

小さい.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tiisasi* (小さし, 'small, tiny, young'), attested in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 小さい

小さな.etymology: Prenominal determiner (rentaishi) derived from 小さなる (*chiisanaru*), formed by analogy with 大きな (from 大きなる) on the stem of 小さい.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 小さな

小窓.etymology: Native Japanese compound of prefix 小- (こ-, 'small') and 窓 (まど, 'window').
小窓.notes: Used for high transom windows and small ventilation casements.

小節.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 小節 (shōsetsu), from Classical Chinese 小節 ('minor matters of conduct, small details, short section'); in modern Japanese music terminology adopted as the translation of 'bar, measure'.

history.meaning: minor point of conduct; small division
musical bar or measure; minor detail

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 小節

小節目.etymology: Compound combining musical term 小節 (shōsetsu, 'bar, measure') + ordinal/point suffix -目 (-me, 'nth, point').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 小節

小脇.etymology: Native Japanese compound prefixing diminutive/light こ- (小) to わき (脇, 'side of the chest, underarm'), used especially in phrases like 小脇に抱える ('tuck under one's arm').

history.meaning: under the arm; side of the torso

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 小脇

小銭.etymology: Compound prefixing native Japanese こ- (小, 'small') to ぜに (銭, Sino-Japanese loan early-natived as 'coin, cash'), meaning 'small coins, small change'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 小銭

小雨.etymology: Native Japanese compound 小雨 (こさめ), from prefix 小- (こ-, 'light, small') + 雨 (あめ, 'rain') with historical medial consonant insertion (-s-).
小雨.notes: The same archaic euphonic -s- before 雨 (あめ -> さめ) appears in 春雨 (はるさめ, 'gentle spring rain') and 秋雨 (あきさめ).

少々.etymology: Sino-Japanese reduplicated adverb/noun 少々 (shōshō), from Chinese 少少 ('a little, slightly'), reduplicating 少 ('few, little').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 少々

少し.etymology: Adverbial and nominalized form derived from the classical adjective すこし (少し, 'small in quantity or degree'), from the same root *suk-* as 少ない (すくない).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 少し

少ない.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sukunasi* (少なし, 'few, scarce, scant'), formed from root *suku-* ('small in number') + adjectival element *-nasi*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 少ない

居場所.etymology: Compound combining い- (居, continuative stem of 居る 'to be, sit, reside') + ばしょ (場所, 'place, location'), meaning 'whereabouts' or 'a place where one belongs'.

history.meaning: place where someone is staying; whereabouts

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 居場所

居心地.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining い- (居, 'sitting, staying, being in a place') + ごこち (心地, rendaku form of ここち 'feeling, sensation').

history.meaning: feeling of comfort when staying in a place
comfort; coziness (of a room or environment)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 居心地

届く.etymology: Intransitive godan verb *todoku* ('to reach, arrive, carry'), attested from Late Middle Japanese; related to とどこほる (滞る) and classical とどく ('to reach the end').

history.meaning: reach a destination; attain; be attentive

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 届く

届ける.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *todokeru* ('to deliver, send, report'), continuing Late Middle Japanese lower bigrade とどく (届く), the transitive counterpart of godan 届く.

history.meaning: cause to reach; deliver; file a report

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 届ける

屋台.etymology: Hybrid/Sino-Japanese compound 屋台 (yatai), combining 屋 (read *ya*, 'roof, shop, house') + 台 (read *tai*, 'platform, stand, cart'), originally a portable roofed float or stage and later a street food stall.

history.meaning: festival float with a roof; mobile street stall
food stall; street cart; festival float

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 屋台

屋根.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining や (屋, 'house, roof') + ね (根, 'base, ridge, upper structural crest'), attested from medieval Japanese as the general word for 'roof' (replacing simple *ya* or *iraka*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 屋根

屋根裏.etymology: Native Japanese compound of 屋根 ('roof', itself 屋 'house' + 根 'covering/base') and 裏 ('underside, back'), literally 'the space underneath the roof'.

屋根裏部屋.etymology: Compound noun formed from やねうら (屋根裏, 'under the roof, attic space', from 屋根 'roof' + 裏 'underside, back') + べや (部屋, 'room').

history.form: 屋根裏部屋 (やねうらべや)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 屋根裏

履く.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *paku* (履く・佩く, 'to put on by slipping the feet or waist into, wear footwear or a sword at the hip'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: wear on the feet or gird at the waist
put on or wear (shoes, trousers, skirts)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 履く

山.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yama* ('mountain, hill, wild forest'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 山

嵐.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *arasi* ('rough mountain wind, storm, tempest'), derived from the verb *aru* / *arasu* (荒る・荒らす, 'to be rough, rage, lay waste').

history.meaning: fierce wind blowing down from mountains; tempest

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 嵐

川.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *kapa* ('river, stream'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, undergoing regular medial *-p- > -f- > -w-* change to modern *kawa*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 川

左.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pidari* ('left, left side'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 左

左側.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining ひだり (左, 'left') + がわ (側, rendaku form of かわ 'side').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 左側

左手.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pidarite* (左手, 'left hand'), combining ひだり (左, 'left') + て (手, 'hand, direction').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 左手

左端.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining ひだり (左, 'left') + はし (端, 'edge, end, extremity').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 左端

左隣.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining ひだり (左, 'left') + どなり (隣, rendaku form of となり 'neighbor, next-door').

history.meaning: next-door on the left; immediate left

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 隣

差す.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sasu* ('to thrust, pierce, insert, point, shine into'), a polysemous verb written with 差す, 指す, 刺す, or 挿す according to nuance.

history.form: さす (差す・指す・刺す)
history.meaning: shine (of sunlight); insert; hold up; point
shine in; hold up (an umbrella); pour/add drops; wear at the belt

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 差す

市.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *iti* ('marketplace, fair, gathering place for trade') and also read Sino-Japanese *shi* (from Middle Chinese 市 *dzyiX*, 'market, city, municipality').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 市

市場.etymology: Compound of 市 ('market, town trade gathering') and 場 ('place, ground'). Read いちば for a physical food or street market where goods change hands directly, and しじょう in broader economic or municipal market contexts.

市役所.etymology: Sino-Japanese administrative compound of 市 ('incorporated city') and 役所 ('public office', from 役 'official duty' + 所 'place'), designating municipal City Hall.

布.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *nuno* ('woven cloth, especially bast-fiber linen/hemp cloth'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 布

帰り.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of かえる (帰る, 'to return, go back home').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 帰り

帰り道.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining かえり (帰り, 'return, returning') + みち (道, 'road, way').

history.meaning: road taken on the way back

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 帰り道

帰る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *kaperu* (帰る・返る, 'to turn back, return to one's point of origin'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 帰る

帳面.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 帳面 (chōmen), combining 帳 ('register, account book, curtain') + 面 ('surface, page'), used since the medieval and Edo periods for a bound paper notebook or ledger.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 帳面

幅.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *faba* (幅, 'width of cloth, breadth'), undergoing medial *-f- > -w- > -b-* nasalized voicing.

history.meaning: width of a bolt of cloth; breadth

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 幅

幅広い.etymology: Native Japanese compound adjective combining はば (幅, 'width, breadth, range') + ひろい (広い, 'wide, broad').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 幅広い

平ら.etymology: Nominal/na-adjectival stem *taira* ('flat, level, even, calm'), attested from Old and Early Middle Japanese (compare 平らか *tairaka* and Heian-kyō 'Capital of Peace and Tranquility'), derived from root *ta-* + derivative suffix *-ira*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 平ら

年.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *to₂si* ('harvest cycle, year, age'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; originally referring to the annual rice crop cycle (compare *tosi-gopi* 'praying for harvest').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 年

年配.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 年配 (nenpai, originally written 年輩), from 年 ('year, age') + 輩 ('generation, peer group, cohort'). From 'approximate age bracket', it specialized to 'advanced in years, elderly'.

history.meaning: elderly; middle-aged or older; around the age of

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 年配

幸運.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 幸運 (kōun), combining 幸 ('good fortune, happiness') + 運 ('fate, luck, destiny').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 幸運

広い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *piro₁si* (広し, 'wide, broad, spacious'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 広い

広げる.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *hirogeru* ('to spread out, unfold, widen, expand'), continuing classical lower bigrade ひろぐ (広ぐ), derived from the root of ひろい (広い).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 広げる

広場.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining the stem ひろ- (広, 'wide, open') + ば (場, 'place, ground'), meaning an open public space or plaza.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 広場

床.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yuka* ('raised floor, platform, bed') and *to₂ko₂* ('sleeping platform, raised alcove, riverbed').

history.meaning: raised wooden floor or sleeping platform

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 床

底.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *so₂ko₂* ('bottom, lowest depth, far extremity'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 底

店主さん.etymology: Polite form combining Sino-Japanese 店主 (tenshu, 'shopkeeper, store owner', from 店 'shop' + 主 'master, proprietor') + honorific suffix -さん.

history.form: 店主さん (てんしゅさん)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 店主

店内.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 店内 (tennai), combining 店 ('shop, store, restaurant') + 内 ('inside, interior').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 店内

店員.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 店員 (ten'in), combining 店 ('shop, store') + 員 ('member, personnel, staff').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 店員

座る.etymology: Inherited from Early Middle Japanese *suwaru* (座る・据わる, 'to settle down in place, sit down'), the intransitive partner of すゑる/すえる (据える, 'to set in place'). Replaced classical ゐる (居る) as the everyday verb for 'to sit'.

history.meaning: be set firmly in place; sit down

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 座る

座面.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 座面 (zamen), combining 座 ('seat, sitting') + 面 ('surface, face'), referring to the seating surface of a chair or stool.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 座面

庭.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *nipa* ('flat open ground, courtyard for ceremonies or work, calm sea surface'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; medial *-p- > -w-* yielded modern *niwa*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 庭

庭用.etymology: Hybrid compound combining native Japanese にわ (庭, 'garden, yard') + Sino-Japanese suffix -よう (用, 'for the use of').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 庭

廊下.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 廊下 (rōka), from Chinese 廊下 ('under the roofed gallery/veranda'), combining 廊 ('covered corridor, colonnade') + 下 ('beneath').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 廊下

建物.etymology: Native Japanese compound *tatemono* formed from the continuative stem たて of たてる (建てる, 'to erect, build') + もの (物, 'thing, structure').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 建物

建築家.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 建築家 (kenchikuka), combining 建築 ('architecture, construction', from 建 'build' + 築 'construct') + specialist suffix -家 (-ka, 'expert, professional').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 建築家

建築規則.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound combining 建築 (kenchiku, 'building, architecture, construction') + 規則 (kisoku, 'regulation, rule, code').

history.form: 建築規則 (けんちくきそく)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 建築

弁護士.etymology: Meiji-era Sino-Japanese legal coinage 弁護士 (bengoshi), officially adopted in the 1893 Attorney Act (弁護士法) to replace 代言人, combining 弁護 ('legal defense, advocacy') + professional suffix -士 ('qualified practitioner').

history.form: 辯護士 / 弁護士 (べんごし)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 弁護士

式.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun and suffix 式 (shiki), from Middle Chinese 式 (*syik*, 'model, rule, ceremony, standard form, formula').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 式

引き.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of ひく (引く, 'to pull, draw, subtract, patronize').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 引き

引き上げる.etymology: Compound verb combining the continuative stem ひき (引き, 'pull, draw') + あげる (上げる, 'raise, lift up').

history.form: 引き上げる (ひきあげる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 引き上げる

引き出し.etymology: Nominalized continuative stem of the compound verb ひきだす (引き出す, 'to pull out, draw out'), lexicalized since the late medieval period for a sliding furniture drawer.

history.meaning: sliding box pulled out from a chest; withdrawal

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 引き出し

引き出す.etymology: Compound verb combining the continuative stem ひき (引き, 'pull, draw') + だす (出す, 'take out, put forth').

history.form: ひきいだす / ひきだす (引き出す)

history.meaning: pull out; draw out; withdraw (money); elicit

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 引き出す

引く.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *piku* (引く・曳く, 'to pull, draw, tug, lead, play a stringed instrument'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: pull; draw; subtract; look up (in a dictionary); catch (a cold)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 引く

引っ越し業者.etymology: Compound noun combining ひっこし (引っ越し, 'moving house, relocation', from 引っ越す) + Sino-Japanese ぎょうしゃ (業者, 'business operator, contractor').

history.form: 引っ越し業者 (ひっこしぎょうしゃ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 引越

弟.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *o₂to₂-uto₂* (弟人, 'younger sibling/person'), a compound of *o₂to₂* ('younger, inferior in birth order', cognate with 劣る *otoru*) + *pito₂* (人, 'person') via sound change *-pito > -uto > -ōto*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 弟

弟さん.etymology: Polite kinship noun formed from おとうと (弟, 'younger brother') + honorific suffix -さん, used to refer respectfully to someone else's younger brother.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 弟

弦.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *turu* ('bowstring, taut cord') and also read Sino-Japanese *gen* (from Middle Chinese 弦 *ɣen*, 'bowstring, string of a musical instrument').

history.meaning: string (of a guitar, violin, or bow)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 弦

張る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *paru* (張る, 'to stretch taut, spread, swell, bud'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: stretch tight (a bowstring or cloth); spread; bud
stretch; pitch (a tent); stick/paste; be expensive

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 張る

強い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tuyosi* (強し, 'strong, mighty, firm, resilient'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 強い

強がる.etymology: Derived godan verb formed from the stem つよ- of 強い ('strong') + verbal suffix -がる (marking outward display of a state or feeling, 'to act as if, put on a show of').

history.meaning: pretend to be tough; put on a brave front

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 強がる

弾く.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *piku* ('to pluck or play a stringed instrument', etymologically identical to 引く 'to pull, draw across strings'), or read *hajiku* ('to flick, snap, repel').

history.meaning: pluck or stroke the strings of a koto or biwa
play (a stringed or keyboard instrument); flick

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 弾く

当たり前.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun and na-adjective formed from あたり (当たり, 'allotted share, what corresponds') + まえ (前, 'portion, due share'), shifting in the Edo period from 'one's proper share' to 'natural, only to be expected, obvious'.

history.form: あたりまへ (当前・当たり前)
history.meaning: one's due portion; what is proper and natural

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 当たり前

当たる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese intransitive verb *ataru* ('to hit, strike against, face, correspond to'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: hit; be exposed to (sun/wind); succeed; be right

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 当たる

当てる.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *ateru* ('to hit, apply, expose to, guess'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade あつ (当つ・充つ), the transitive partner of あたる (当たる).

history.meaning: apply to; press against; assign; hit

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 当てる

当館.etymology: Sino-Japanese formal compound 当館 (tōkan), combining proximal/reflexive prefix 当 ('this, our') + 館 ('hall, inn, museum, building').

history.meaning: this inn/hotel; this museum/library; our establishment

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 当館

彫る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *poru* (彫る・掘る, 'to dig out, hollow out, carve, engrave'); originally a single verb written 掘る for digging earth and 彫る for carving wood, stone, or metal.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 彫る

影.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *kage₂* ('light, reflection, visual image, silhouette, shade/shadow'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; originally denoted both gleaming light/reflection and the dark shadow cast by an object.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 影

役.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 役 (yaku / eki), from Middle Chinese 役 (*jwek*, 'corvée labor, military service, official duty'); in Japanese extended to 'assigned office, role, dramatic part, usefulness'.

history.meaning: role; part (in a play); position; service/use

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 役

役所.etymology: Compound combining Sino-Japanese やく (役, 'public office, official duty') + しょ (所, 'place, office'), attested from medieval Japanese for a post of official duty or government office.

history.meaning: post of official duty; magistrate's or government office
government office; public office; municipal hall

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 役所

彼.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese distal demonstrative *kare* (彼, 'that thing or person over there', formed from distal root *ka-* + suffix *-re*). Under Western translation influence in the Meiji era, it specialized as the third-person masculine pronoun 'he' (and 'boyfriend').

history.meaning: that one over there; that person

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 彼

彼ら.etymology: Third-person plural pronoun formed from 彼 (kare, 'that person; he') + pluralizing suffix -ら (等, from Old Japanese *-ra*). Attested since classical times for 'those people' and used in modern Japanese for 'they, them'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 彼ら

往復.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 往復 (ōfuku), from Classical Chinese 往復 ('going and returning'), combining 往 ('go') + 復 ('return').

history.meaning: round trip; going and returning; correspondence

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 往復

待つ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *matu* (待つ, 'to wait for, await, expect'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 待つ

後.etymology: Read both as *ato* (from Old Japanese *ato* 'footprint, track, behind, after') and *nochi* (from Old Japanese *no₂ti* 'later time, future, posterity'), as well as Sino-Japanese *go / kō*.

history.form: 後 (あと / のち / ご)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 後

後ろ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *usiro₁* (後ろ, 'back side, space behind, rear'), formed from the root *usi-* (possibly related to *ura* 'back') + locative noun suffix *-ro₁*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 後ろ

後半.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 後半 (kōhan), combining 後 ('latter, behind, after') + 半 ('half'), meaning 'the second half, latter half'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 後半

心臓.etymology: Sino-Japanese anatomical compound 心臓 (shinzō), from traditional Chinese medicine 五臓 (the five viscera), combining 心 ('heart') + 臓 ('internal organ, viscus').

history.meaning: the heart organ among the five viscera

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 心臓

心配.etymology: Japanese-coined or Early Modern Sino-Japanese compound 心配 (shinpai), combining 心 ('mind, heart') + 配 ('distribute, deploy, pay attention to' — compare native 気を配る 'to pay attention, be on guard').

history.meaning: putting one's mind to every detail; anxiety; care

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 心配

必ず.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese adverb *kanarazu* (必ず, 'without fail, certainly, necessarily'), lexicalized from the negative form *kanarazu* of a defective verb *kanaru* ('to be tentative/partial' or related to 兼ねる 'to hold two possibilities').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 必ず

必要.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 必要 (hitsuyō), from Classical/Tang Chinese 必要 ('indispensable, must-have'), combining 必 ('certainly, inevitably') + 要 ('essential, need').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 必要

忘れる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *wasuru* (忘る, 'to let slip from the mind, forget'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, becoming modern ichidan *wasureru*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 忘れる

忘れ物センター.etymology: Modern hybrid compound combining わすれもの (忘れ物, 'lost article, item left behind', from 忘れる + 物) + loanword センター (from English *center*).

history.form: 忘れ物センター (わすれものセンター)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 忘れ物

快適.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 快適 (kaiteki), from Chinese 快適 ('pleasant and agreeable'), combining 快 ('pleasant, refreshing') + 適 ('fit, comfortable, agreeable').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 快適

怒る.etymology: Read both as *okoru* (originally 興る・起こる 'to rise up, flare up' of temper, applied to 怒る in Early Modern Japanese) and *ikaru* (inherited from Old Japanese *ikaru* 'to bristle with rage, become furious').

history.meaning: lose one's temper; get angry; scold

history.form: 怒る (おこる / いかる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 怒る

怒鳴る.etymology: Early Modern Japanese compound verb *donaru* ('to shout, bellow, yell angrily'), formed from a reinforced prefix ど- (度 / 怒) + なる (鳴る, 'to sound, roar, ring out'), later spelled ateji-style with 怒 ('anger').

history.form: どなる (度鳴る・怒鳴る)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 怒鳴る

怖い.etymology: Shifted in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese from classical こはし (強し・剛し, 'hard, stiff, unyielding, intimidating') to 'frightening, scary, fearful'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 怖い

思い出.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from the continuative stem おもひで of the classical verb おもひいづ / おもひづ (思ひ出づ, 'to come to mind, recall, recollect').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 思い出

思い出す.etymology: Compound godan verb combining the continuative stem おもい (思い, 'think, feel') + だす (出す, 'bring out, call forth'), replacing earlier lower bigrade 思ひ出づ.

history.form: おもひいだす / おもひだす (思ひ出す)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 思い出す

思う.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *o₂mo₂pu* (思ふ, 'to think, feel in one's heart, love, yearn for'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; often connected with おも (面, 'face, expression').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 思う

急ぐ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *iso₁gu* (急ぐ, 'to prepare busily, hasten, hurry'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 急ぐ

急便.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 急便 (kyūbin), combining 急 ('urgent, rapid, express') + 便 ('dispatch, mail/courier service').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 急便

急須.etymology: Borrowed from early modern southern Chinese (Min / Wu pronunciation of 急須 or 急焼, a small vessel for quickly warming wine or steeping tea), adopted in Edo-period sencha culture for a small side-handled teapot.

history.meaning: small quick-heating pot for wine or tea

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 急須

恥ずかしい.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *padukasi* (恥づかし, 'admirable to the point of making one feel inadequate; bashful; ashamed'), derived from the verb はづ (恥づ, modern 恥じる 'to feel shame').

history.meaning: so impressive as to humble the observer; bashful; shameful

history.form: 恥ずかしい (はずかしい)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 恥ずかしい

息.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *oki₁* > *iki₁* ('breath, respiration, vital spirit'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; cognate with いく (生く, 'to live').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 息

息切れ.etymology: Native Japanese compound noun combining いき (息, 'breath') + ぎれ (切れ, rendaku form of きれ from 切れる 'to run out, be cut off').

history.meaning: shortness of breath; panting; running out of steam

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 息切れ

悩み.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of なやむ (悩む, Old Japanese *nayamu* 'to suffer illness, ache, be troubled or distressed').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 悩み

悪い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *warusi* (悪し, 'inferior, poor in quality, undesirable, bad'), attested in the Man'yōshū; gradually took over the semantic territory of classical あし (悪し).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 悪い

意味.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 意味 (imi), from Classical and Buddhist Chinese 意味 ('thought and flavor; underlying significance, purport, meaning').

history.meaning: import and flavor of words; meaning

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 意味

意地.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 意地 (iji), originally a Buddhist term translating Sanskrit *manobhūmi* ('the ground/plane of mind and thought'); in Early Modern Japanese it shifted to 'disposition, stubborn pride, willpower'.

history.meaning: stubbornness; pride; willpower; appetite (in 意地が汚い)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 意地

感じ.etymology: Deverbal noun formed from the continuative stem of the Sino-Japanese suru/zuru-verb 感ず / 感じる (from Middle Chinese 感 'to be moved, feel, sense').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 感じ

感傷.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 感傷 (kanshō), from Classical Chinese 感傷 ('to be moved to sorrow, feel sentimental grief'), combining 感 ('be moved, feel') + 傷 ('wound, grieve').
