sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 感傷

慌てる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *awatu* (慌つ, 'to be flustered, lose one's composure, panic'), attested in the Nihon Shoki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: be flustered; be thrown into confusion
hurry in confusion; panic; be flustered

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 慌てる

懐中電灯.etymology: Meiji/Taishō-era Sino-Japanese compound 懐中電灯 (kaichū dentō), combining 懐中 ('inside the breast pocket, pocket-sized') + 電灯 ('electric lamp/light').

history.form: 懐中電灯 (かいちゅうでんとう)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 懐中電灯

戻す.etymology: Transitive godan verb *modosu* ('to put back, return, restore, vomit'), paired with intransitive もどる (戻る).

history.meaning: turn back; restore to an earlier state

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 戻す

戻る.etymology: Intransitive godan verb *modoru* ('to turn back, return'), attested in classical Japanese in the sense 'to twist back, go against, turn around', whence 'to return to a point of departure'.

history.meaning: go counter to; twist back; return

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 戻る

所.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *to₂ko₂ro₂* (所・処, 'place, spot, locality'), formed from spatial root *to₂ko₂* (compare 床 'bed/platform') + suffix *-ro₂*.

history.meaning: place; spot; aspect; just about to

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 所

扇風機.etymology: Meiji/Taishō Sino-Japanese coinage 扇風機 (せんぷうき), combining 扇 ('fan, stir breeze'), 風 ('wind'), and 機 ('machine').
扇風機.notes: Coined in Japan for early electric fans and adopted across East Asia (compare Korean 선풍기).

手.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *te* (compound combining form *ta-*, 'hand, arm, skill, handwriting, means'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: hand; arm; effort; means; move (in games)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 手

手仕事.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining て (手, 'hand') + しごと (仕事, 'work, craft'), meaning manual craftwork or handiwork.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 手仕事

手伝う.etymology: Compound verb *tetsudau* ('to lend a hand, help, assist'), formed from て (手, 'hand') + つたふ/つたう (伝う, 'to go along, pass along, assist').

history.meaning: lend a hand; assist in work

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 手伝う

手元.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining て (手, 'hand') + もと (元・下, 'base, near at hand, vicinity').

history.meaning: close to one's hands; in one's possession; reach
at hand; on hand; one's grip or purse

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 手元

手入れ.etymology: Nominalized continuative stem of the phrase/compound てをいれる / ていれる (手を入れる, 'to put one's hand in -> to mend, care for, trim, or raid').

history.meaning: maintenance; care; upkeep; pruning; police raid

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 手入れ

手帳.etymology: Hybrid compound combining native Japanese て (手, 'hand, at hand') + Sino-Japanese ちょう (帳, 'register, bound notebook'), denoting a small pocket notebook.

history.meaning: pocket notebook; planner; official certificate book

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 手帳

手書き.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining て (手, 'hand') + がき (書き, rendaku form of かき from 書く 'to write, draw').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 手書き

手紙.etymology: Native Japanese compound of 手 (*te*, 'hand, handwriting') and 紙 (*kami* -> *-gami* via rendaku, 'paper'), shifting from a handy slip of note paper to any written letter.

手違い.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining て (手, 'hand, procedure, move') + ちがい (違い, 'discrepancy, mistake', from 違う).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 手違い

才能.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 才能 (sainō), from Classical Chinese 才能 ('natural endowment and practical ability, talent'), combining 才 ('innate gift') + 能 ('capability').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 才能

打つ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *utu* (打つ・撃つ・討つ, 'to strike, beat, hit, pound'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: hit; strike; beat; type; drive (a nail)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 打つ

払う.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *parapu* (払ふ・祓ふ, 'to sweep away, clear away, ritualistically purify'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; later extended to 'clear an account, pay'.

history.meaning: brush off; settle and pay a bill
pay; brush away; wipe off; pay (attention/respect)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 払う

払える.etymology: Potential ichidan form (*haraeru*, 'can pay, be able to pay') derived from the godan verb はらう (払う, 'to pay, brush away').

history.meaning: be able to pay; can afford to pay

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 払う

扱う.etymology: Inherited from Classical Japanese *atukafu* (扱ふ, 'to busy oneself with, manage, mediate, handle'), becoming modern *atsukau*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 扱う

折りたたみ.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of おりたたむ (折り畳む, 'to fold up'), used as a noun or modifier for collapsible/folding items.

history.form: 折りたたみ / 折り畳み (おりたたみ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 折り畳み

折りたたみ椅子.etymology: Compound noun combining おりたたみ (折りたたみ, 'folding, collapsible') + いす (椅子, 'chair').

history.form: 折りたたみ椅子 (おりたたみいす)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 折り畳み椅子

折りたたむ.etymology: Compound godan verb combining the continuative stem おり (折り, from 折る 'to bend, fold') + たたむ (畳む, 'to fold up neatly, collapse').

history.form: 折りたたむ / 折り畳む (おりたたむ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 折り畳む

折る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese transitive verb *woru* (折る, 'to bend, snap, break off, fold'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; initial *w-* before *o* disappeared in Middle Japanese.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 折る

折れる.etymology: Intransitive ichidan verb *oreru* ('to break, snap, be folded, give in'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade をる (折る), the intransitive partner of godan 折る.

history.meaning: break; snap; be folded; turn (a corner); compromise

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 折れる

抜く.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese transitive verb *nuku* (抜く・貫く, 'to pull out, extract, pierce through, omit'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: draw out; pull out; pass through
pull out; extract; remove; overtake; omit

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 抜く

抜ける.etymology: Intransitive ichidan verb *nukeru* ('to come out, fall out, pass through, be missing'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade ぬく (抜く), the intransitive partner of godan 抜く.

history.meaning: come loose; slip out; pass through
come out; fall out; pass through; be left out

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 抜ける

抱える.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *kakaeru* ('to hold or carry in one's arms, embrace, employ, bear a problem'), continuing Classical Japanese lower bigrade かかふ (抱ふ), related to かく (掛く・懸く).

history.meaning: hold in the arms; retain; support
hold under or in one's arms; carry; have (problems/staff)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 抱える

押さえる.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *osaえる* ('to press down, hold steady, restrain, grasp'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade おさふ (押さふ・抑ふ), derived from the same root *os-* as 押す.

history.meaning: press down and hold; check; restrain
hold down; press; secure; grasp (the main point)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 押さえる

押す.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *osu* (押す・推す, 'to push, press, exert force upon'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 押す

担当.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 担当 (tantō), from Chinese 擔當 ('to shoulder and take charge of'), combining 担 (擔, 'carry on the shoulders, bear') + 当 (當, 'face, take on').

history.meaning: being in charge; person in charge; responsibility

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 担当

担当者.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound combining 担当 (tantō, 'being in charge, handling') + agentive suffix -者 (-sha, 'person').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 担当者

拭き跡.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining ふき (拭き, continuative stem of 拭く 'to wipe') + あと (跡, 'mark, trace, streak').

history.meaning: wipe mark; streak left after wiping

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 拭く

拭く.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *puku* ('to wipe, rub clean, dry with a cloth'), attested in Early Middle Japanese dictionaries alongside Old Japanese *nugupu* (拭ふ).

history.meaning: wipe away moisture or dirt with a cloth

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 拭く

持ち上げる.etymology: Compound verb combining the continuative stem もち (持ち, from 持つ 'to hold') + あげる (上げる, 'to raise, lift up'); also used figuratively for 'to flatter'.

history.meaning: lift up in one's hands; praise highly

history.form: 持ち上げる (もちあげる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 持ち上げる

持ち主.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining もち (持ち, 'holding, possessing') + ぬし (主, 'master, owner').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 持ち主

持ち手.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining もち (持ち, 'holding, carrying') + て (手, 'hand; handle; person who does').

history.meaning: handle; grip; strap (of a bag); bearer/owner

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 持ち手

持ち歩く.etymology: Compound godan verb combining もち (持ち, 'hold, carry') + あるく (歩く, 'walk, go about').

history.form: もちありく / もちあるく (持ち歩く)

history.meaning: carry around; carry on one's person

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 持ち歩く

持つ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mo₂tu* (持つ, 'to take in the hand, hold, carry, possess'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: hold in the hand; carry; possess

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 持つ

指.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yubi₁* (earlier also *oyobi₁*, 'finger, toe'), attested in the Kojiki and Wamyō Ruijushō.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 指

指さす.etymology: Compound godan verb combining ゆび (指, 'finger') + さす (指す, 'to point at, indicate').

history.form: ゆびさす (指さす・指差す)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 指さす

指す.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sasu* (指す・差す, 'to point toward, indicate, aim for, nominate'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 指す

指図.etymology: Sino-Japanese / hybrid medieval compound 指図 (sashizu), combining 指 ('point with the finger, indicate') + 図 ('plan, diagram'). Originally 'pointing out on a plan; architectural blueprint' in Kamakura/Muromachi usage, whence 'directions, orders, instructions'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 指図

挟まる.etymology: Intransitive godan verb *hasamaru* ('to get caught between, be sandwiched'), derived from transitive はさむ (挟む, Old Japanese *pasamu* 'to hold between two surfaces, pinch') + intransitive suffix *-aru*.

history.meaning: hold or press between two things
get caught between; be wedged; be sandwiched

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 挟まる

挨拶.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 挨拶 (aisatsu), from Zen Buddhist Chinese 挨拶 ('pressing forward and pushing against one another' — testing a disciple's awakening through verbal exchange), which broadened in Early Modern Japanese to 'polite exchange, greeting, salutation'.

history.meaning: exchange of probing questions and answers between master and monk

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 挨拶

振る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *puru* (振る, 'to wave, shake, swing, brandish'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: wave; shake; swing; sprinkle; reject (a suitor); assign (a role)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 振る

捨てる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *sutu* (棄つ・捨つ, 'to cast away, abandon, discard'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, becoming modern ichidan *suteru*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 捨てる

掃除.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 掃除 (sōji), from Classical Chinese 掃除 ('to sweep away dirt and put in order'), combining 掃 ('sweep with a broom') + 除 ('remove, clear away').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 掃除

掛かる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese intransitive verb *kakaru* (掛かる・懸かる, 'to hang, be suspended, catch on, begin, require'), paired with transitive かく / かける (掛ける).

history.form: かかる (掛かる・懸かる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 掛かる

掛ける.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *kakeru* ('to hang, suspend, put on, multiply, spend, call'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade かく (掛く・懸く).

history.meaning: hang up; suspend; rest one thing upon another
hang; put on (glasses); sit in (a chair); make (a phone call); multiply

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 掛ける

探す.etymology: Inherited from Classical Japanese *sagasu* (探す・捜す, 'to search for, look for'), closely related to Old Japanese さぐる (探る, 'to grope for, probe').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 探す

揃う.etymology: Intransitive godan verb *sorou* ('to become complete, match, gather together uniformly'), continuing Late Middle Japanese そろふ (揃ふ), paired with transitive そろえる (揃える).

history.meaning: be uniform; be complete as a set; gather

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 揃う

描く.etymology: Read both as *egaku* (derived from Old Japanese ゑがく 絵描く, from ゑ 'picture, painting' + かく 'scratch, draw') and *kaku* (same native verb as 書く, specialized in orthography to drawing pictures).

history.meaning: draw lines or paint a picture

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 描く

提灯.etymology: Muromachi-period tōon (唐音, Song/Ming Chinese) borrowing 提灯 (ちょうちん, originally ていちん), literally 'hand-carried lamp' (提 'carry in hand' + 灯 'lantern').
提灯.notes: Its tōon reading ちょうちん (rather than kan'on ていとう) marks its arrival with medieval Zen and merchant trade.

改めて.etymology: Lexicalized adverb formed from the conjunctive (-te) form of the transitive verb あらためる (改める, 'to renew, change, do over'), from the root of あらた (新た, 'new, fresh').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 改めて

改装.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 改装 (kaisō), combining 改 ('change, renew, alter') + 装 ('dress, outfit, interior/exterior fitting').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 改装

救い出す.etymology: Compound godan verb combining the continuative stem すくい (救い, from 救う 'to save, rescue') + だす (出す, 'to take out, bring out').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 救い出す

救う.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sukupu* (救ふ・掬ふ, 'to scoop up out of water or danger, rescue, save, relieve'), attested in the Nihon Shoki and Man'yōshū; etymologically the same verb as 掬う ('to scoop up').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 救う

救世主.etymology: Sino-Japanese religious compound 救世主 (kyūseishu), combining 救世 ('saving the world', originally a Buddhist epithet of bodhisattvas such as Guanyin/Kannon) + 主 ('lord, master'), adopted in Christian translation for 'Savior, Messiah'.

history.form: 救世主 (きゅうせいしゅ)
history.meaning: Savior of the world; Messiah; lifesaver

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 救世主

教える.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *osipu* (教ふ, 'to point out, instruct, teach, tell'), becoming modern ichidan *oshieru*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 教える

数分.etymology: Sino-Japanese numerical expression 数分 (sūfun), combining prefixal 数 ('several, a few') + counter 分 ('minute').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 数分

数字.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 数字 (sūji), combining 数 ('number, count') + 字 ('written character, figure').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 数字

整える.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *totonoeru* ('to put in order, arrange, prepare, adjust'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade ととのふ (整ふ・調ふ), paired with intransitive ととのう (整う).

history.meaning: bring into harmony or order; arrange; prepare
put in order; arrange; tidy up; prepare

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 整える

敷く.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *siku* (敷く, 'to spread out flat, lay down a mat, cover, extend dominion over'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: spread out; lay down (mats); rule over
spread out; lay (a futon, rug, or rails)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 敷く

文.etymology: Sino-Japanese *bun / mon* (from Middle Chinese 文 *mjun*, 'pattern, written character, writing, sentence') and native Japanese *fumi* (an early borrowing from Middle Chinese 文 *mjun*, meaning 'written document, letter').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 文

文化財課.etymology: Sino-Japanese administrative compound combining 文化財 (bunkazai, 'cultural property/heritage', codified by the 1950 Law for the Protection of Cultural Properties) + 課 (ka, 'municipal division/section').

history.form: 文化財課 (ぶんかざいか)
history.meaning: Cultural Properties Division (in a municipal or prefectural office)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 文化財

文字.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 文字 (moji / monji), from Classical Chinese 文字 ('written graphs and characters'), combining 文 ('simple pictographic graph') + 字 ('compound character').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 文字

文章.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 文章 (bunshō), from Classical Chinese 文章 ('patterned ornament; literary composition'), shifting in Japanese from 'literary work' to 'prose text, composition, sentence(s)'.

history.meaning: ornate pattern; literary prose or verse

history.form: もんじゃう / ぶんしゃう (文章)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 文章

断る.etymology: Inherited from Classical Japanese *kotowaru* (理る・断る, 'to explain the reason, judge, give prior notice, excuse oneself'), derived from ことわり (理・断り, 'reason, principle, explanation', from 事 'matter' + 割る 'divide/distinguish').

history.meaning: state the reason; judge; give advance notice
refuse; decline; ask leave/give notice in advance

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 断る

新しい.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *aratasi* ('fresh, new'), which underwent consonant metathesis (*r...t* > *t...r*) in the Heian period to become *atarasi* > modern 新しい (*atarashii*).

新人.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 新人 (shinjin), from Classical Chinese 新人 ('new person, bride, newcomer'), combining 新 ('new') + 人 ('person').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 新人

新品.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 新品 (shinpin), combining 新 ('new') + 品 ('article, goods, item').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 新品

新聞紙.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 新聞 ('newspaper', literally 'newly heard things') and 紙 ('paper'), referring specifically to sheets of newsprint.

新鮮.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 新鮮 (shinsen), from Classical Chinese 新鮮 ('fresh and bright, newly harvested or caught'), combining 新 ('new') + 鮮 ('fresh, vivid').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 新鮮

方.etymology: Read both as native Japanese *kata* (inherited from Old Japanese *kata* 'direction, side, way, respected person') and Sino-Japanese *hō* (from Middle Chinese 方 *pjang*, 'direction, side, comparison').

history.meaning: person (polite), way of doing (kata); direction, side of a comparison (hō)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 方

旅.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tabi₁* (旅, 'journey, temporary stay away from home'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 旅

旅行.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 旅行 (ryokō), from Classical Chinese 旅行 ('traveling away from home'), combining 旅 ('travel, sojourn') + 行 ('go, walk, journey').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 旅行

旅行ガイド.etymology: Modern hybrid compound combining Sino-Japanese 旅行 (ryokō, 'travel, trip') + loanword ガイド (from English *guide*).

history.form: 旅行ガイド (りょこうガイド)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 旅行

旅館.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 旅 ('travel, journey') and 館 ('hall, mansion, lodging house'), naming a traditional Japanese inn.

日.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pi₁* (combining form *ka-*, 'sun, daytime, day'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; also read Sino-Japanese *nichi / jitsu* (from Middle Chinese 日 *nyit*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 日

日付.etymology: Native Japanese compound *hiduke* ('date written on a document'), combining ひ (日, 'day') + づけ (付け, rendaku form of つけ 'attaching, writing down').

history.meaning: inscribing the date on a document; date

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 日付

日差し.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining ひ (日, 'sun, sunlight') + ざし (差し, rendaku form of さし from 差す 'to shine in, beam').

history.form: ひざし (日差し・日射し)
history.meaning: shining of the sun; rays of sunlight
sunlight; sunbeams; rays of the sun

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 日差し

日当たり.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining ひ (日, 'sun, sunlight') + あたり (当たり, from 当たる 'to strike, shine upon').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 日当たり

日曜日.etymology: Compound 日曜日 (nichiyōbi, 'Sunday'), combining 日曜 ('day of the Sun', from classical astrological 七曜 'seven luminaries') + 日 ('day'). Adopted as the official calendar day name in the Meiji era.

history.meaning: Day of the Sun (in the seven-luminary cycle)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 日曜日

旧市街.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 旧市街 (kyūshigai), combining 旧 ('old, former, historic') + 市街 ('city streets, urban area'), used for the historic old town of a city.

history.meaning: old town; historic quarter of a city

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 市街

早い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *payasi* (早し・速し, 'early, swift, rapid'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: early in time; swift in motion

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 早い

昇進.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 昇進 (shōshin), from Classical Chinese 昇進 ('to rise and advance in official rank'), combining 昇 ('ascend, rise') + 進 ('advance').

history.meaning: ascend in court rank or office

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 昇進

明かり.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of the Old Japanese verb あかる (明かる, 'to grow bright, dawn'), denoting light, illumination, or a lamp.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 明かり

明るい.etymology: Derived in Late Middle and Early Modern Japanese as an i-adjective from the verb あかる (明かる, 'to grow bright, lighten') + adjectival -い, replacing earlier あかし (明かし, 'bright, clear').

history.form: あかし (明かし) / あかる (明かる)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 明るい

明日.etymology: Read both as native Japanese *ashita* (from Old Japanese *asita* 'morning, the morning of the next day') or *asu* (from Old Japanese *asu* 'tomorrow'), and Sino-Japanese *myōnichi*.

history.form: あす (明日) / あした (朝・明日)
明日 (あした / あす / みょうにち)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 明日

昔.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mukasi* (昔, 'olden times, the past'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; often connected with むかふ (向かふ, 'to face toward').

history.meaning: olden days; the past; former times

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 昔

星.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *po₂si* (星, 'star, heavenly body'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; often compared internally with *pi* (火・日, 'fire, light').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 星

映える.etymology: Intransitive ichidan verb *haeru* (or *baeru* in recent colloquial slang), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade はゆ (映ゆ・栄ゆ, 'to shine forth, look radiant, stand out attractively').

history.meaning: shine brightly; look splendid by contrast
shine; look attractive; stand out favorably

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 映える

春.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *paru* (春, 'spring season'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; traditionally associated with はる (張る, 'buds swelling/stretching') or はる (晴る, 'skies clearing').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 春

昨夜.etymology: Read both as Sino-Japanese *sakuya* (combining 昨 'yesterday, last' + 夜 'night') and native Japanese *yūbe* (from ゆふべ 夕べ, 'evening, last night').

history.form: 昨夜 (さくや / ゆうべ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 昨夜

昨日.etymology: Read both as native Japanese *kinō* (inherited from Old Japanese *ki₁no₂pu* 'yesterday', undergoing *-pu > -fu > -u > -ō*) and formal Sino-Japanese *sakujitsu*.

history.form: 昨日 (きのう / さくじつ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 昨日

昼.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pi₁ru* (昼, 'daytime, midday, noon'), formed from the root *pi₁* (日, 'sun, day') + temporal suffix *-ru* (compare *yo₁ru* 夜).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 昼

時.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *to₂ki₁* (時, 'time, season, occasion, hour'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 時

時々.etymology: Reduplicated native Japanese temporal noun/adverb *tokidoki* (時々, from Old Japanese *to₂ki₁* 'time'), meaning 'from time to time, at times, sometimes'.

history.meaning: at each season; from time to time

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 時々

時刻表.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 時刻表 (jikokuhyō), combining 時刻 ('time of day, hour and minute') + 表 ('table, chart, schedule').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 時刻表

時期.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 時期 (jiki), from Classical Chinese 時期 ('appointed time, season'), combining 時 ('time, season') + 期 ('period, appointed time').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 時期

時点.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 時点 (jiten), combining 時 ('time') + 点 ('point, spot'), modeling 'point in time'.

history.meaning: point in time; juncture; as of

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 時点

時計.etymology: Compound of 時 ('time, hour') and 計 ('measure, gauge'). Historically read どけい from 土圭 ('sundial') and reanalyzed with 計 ('timepiece, meter') as tokei.

時計台.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 時計台 (tokeidai), combining 時計 ('clock, timepiece', originally *tokei* from 土圭 'sundial' + 計 'measure') + 台 ('tower, stand, pedestal').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 時計台

時計職人.etymology: Compound joining 時計 (とけい, 'clock, watch') and 職人 (しょくにん, 'skilled artisan, master craftsperson').
時計職人.notes: Evokes precision handiwork with tiny pins, springs, and tweezers.

時間.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 時 ('time, hour, season') and 間 ('interval, space between'), denoting either a span of hours or time in general.

普段.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 普段 (fudan, originally written 不断), from Buddhist and Classical Chinese 不断 ('unceasing, continuous, without interruption'); shifted in Japanese from 'always, continually' to 'ordinary times, usual, everyday'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 普段

普通.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 普通 (futsū), from Classical and Buddhist Chinese 普通 ('universally pervading, general, common to all'), combining 普 ('universal, widespread') + 通 ('pass through, common').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 普通

景色.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 景色 (keshiki, earlier also *keishoku*), from Chinese 景色 ('light and color of a scene; scenery'), combining 景 ('sunlight, view, scene') + 色 ('color, appearance').

history.meaning: appearance of light and nature; scenery

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 景色

晴れ.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of はれる (晴れる, classical はる 'to clear up, be dispelled, be open and public').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 晴れ

晴れる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *paru* (晴る・霽る, 'for clouds, fog, or gloom to clear away; to become open and bright'), becoming modern ichidan *hareru*.

history.meaning: clear up (of sky or mist); be dispelled (of doubt)
clear up; be sunny; feel refreshed

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 晴れる

暖かい.etymology: Adjectival derivative formed from the classical naru-adjective あたたかなり (暖かなり・温かなり, 'warm, mild, genial'), shifting to an i-adjective in Late Middle Japanese; spelled 暖かい specifically for weather, air, or colors.

history.form: あたたかなり (暖かなり)

history.meaning: warm; mild (of weather or climate); genial

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 暖かい

暖房.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 暖房 (danbō), from Chinese 暖房 ('warm room; warming a chamber'), combining 暖 ('warm') + 房 ('room, chamber').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 暖房

暗い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *kurasi* (暗し, 'dark, dim, unlit, gloomy'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; cognate with くる (暮る, 'to grow dark') and くろ (黒, 'black').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 暗い

暮らす.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese transitive/temporal verb *kurasu* (暮らす, 'to spend the day until dark, pass time'), derived from くる (暮る, 'for the sun to set, grow dark'); later generalized to 'to make a living, live one's daily life'.

history.meaning: live; make a living; pass one's days

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 暮らす

曲.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 曲 (kyoku), from Middle Chinese 曲 (*kʰjowk*, 'bent, crooked; winding melody, tune, song').

history.meaning: bend; twist; musical tune or song
tune; piece of music; song; curve/twist

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 曲

曲がり角.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining まがり (曲がり, continuative stem of 曲がる 'to turn, bend') + かど (角, 'corner, angle').

history.meaning: street corner; bend in the road; turning point

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 曲がり角

曲がる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese intransitive verb *magaru* (曲がる, 'to bend, curve, turn, be crooked'), paired with transitive まぐ/まげる (曲げる).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 曲がる

書き留める.etymology: Compound ichidan verb combining the continuative stem かき (書き, from 書く 'to write') + とめる (留める, 'to fix in place, keep, record').

history.meaning: set down in writing to preserve

history.form: 書き留める (かきとめる)
history.meaning: write down; jot down; make a note of

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 書き留める

書く.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *kaku* ('to scratch, incise, draw lines, paint, write characters'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; etymologically the same verb as 掻く ('to scratch') and 描く ('to draw').

history.form: かく (書く・描く・掻く)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 書く

書斎.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 書斎 (shosai), from Classical Chinese 書齋 ('quiet room for reading and writing, study'), combining 書 ('books, writing') + 斎 (齋, 'quiet studio, study chamber').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 書斎

書留.etymology: Nominalized form of かきとめ (書き留め, from 書き留める 'to record in writing'), adopted in the modern Japanese postal system for 'registered mail' (because the sender and recipient are recorded in the ledger).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 書留

書類.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 書類 (shorui), combining 書 ('written document, paper') + 類 ('category, class, collection of items').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 書類

替える.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *kaeru* ('to replace, substitute, exchange'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade かふ (替ふ・代ふ・換ふ), spelled 替える specifically when replacing one thing with another.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 替える

最初.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 最初 (saisho), from Buddhist and Classical Chinese 最初 ('the very beginning, first of all'), combining superlative prefix 最 ('most') + 初 ('beginning, first').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 最初

最後.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 最後 (saigo), from Classical Chinese 最後 ('the very last, furthest behind'), combining superlative 最 ('most') + 後 ('after, behind, last').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 最後

最新.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 最新 (saishin), combining superlative prefix 最 ('most') + 新 ('new').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 最新

最終日.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 最終日 (saishūbi), combining 最終 ('final, last', from 最 'most' + 終 'end') + 日 ('day').

history.meaning: final day; last day; closing day

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 最終日

最高.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 最高 (saikō), from Classical Chinese 最高 ('highest, supreme'), combining superlative 最 ('most') + 高 ('high, tall').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 最高

月.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tuki₂* (月, 'moon, month'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; also read Sino-Japanese *getsu / gatsu* (from Middle Chinese 月 *ngjwot*).

history.form: 月 (つき / げつ / がつ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 月

月曜.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 月曜 (getsuyō), literally 'luminary of the Moon' from the classical astrological七曜 (seven-planet week), serving as the short form of 月曜日 ('Monday').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 月曜

月曜日.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 月曜日 (getsuyōbi), combining 月曜 ('Day of the Moon') + 日 ('day').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 月曜日

月末.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 月末 (getsumatsu), combining 月 ('month') + 末 ('end, tip'), denoting the end of the month.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 月末

有塩バター.etymology: Modern culinary compound combining Sino-Japanese 有塩 (yūen, 'salted, containing salt', from 有 'have' + 塩 'salt') + loanword バター (from English *butter*).

history.form: 有塩バター (ゆうえんバター)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — バター

朝.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *asa* (朝, 'morning'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; cognate with あす (明日, 'tomorrow') and あした (朝, 'morning').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 朝

朝ごはん.etymology: Compound combining native Japanese あさ (朝, 'morning') + ごはん (ご飯, polite prefix ご- + 飯 'cooked rice, meal').

history.form: 朝ごはん / 朝御飯 (あさごはん)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 朝御飯

朝カフェ.etymology: Modern colloquial hybrid compound combining native Japanese あさ (朝, 'morning') + loanword カフェ (from French *café*), referring to visiting a café in the morning for coffee or breakfast.

history.meaning: morning café visit; breakfast at a café

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — カフェ

木.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ki₂* (combining form *ko₂-*, 'tree, wood, timber'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.form: 木 (き / もく / ぼく)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 木

木工ボンド.etymology: Hybrid compound combining Sino-Japanese 木工 (mokkō, 'woodworking, carpentry', from 木 'wood' + 工 'craft') + loanword ボンド (from English *bond*, popularized in Japan by Konishi Co.'s trademarked polyvinyl acetate wood glue).

history.form: 木工ボンド (もっこうボンド)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 木工

木曜日.etymology: Compound of 木曜 ('Jupiter day', linked to the Five Phases element 木 'wood/tree') and 日 ('day') in the traditional East Asian planetary week.

木枠.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining き (木, 'wood, timber') + わく (枠, 'frame, reel, border').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 木枠

木目.etymology: Hybrid reading もくめ combining Sino-Japanese 木 (もく, 'wood, timber') with native 目 (め, 'eye, pattern, grain').
木目.notes: Native 目 productively denotes fine surface patterns in 網目 ('mesh'), 織り目 ('weave'), and 木目 ('wood grain').

木箱.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining き (木, 'wood') + はこ (箱, 'box, case, chest').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 木箱

未完成.etymology: Sino-Japanese prefix 未- (み-, 'not yet') attached to 完成 (かんせい, 'completion': 完 'whole' + 成 'accomplish').
未完成.notes: Unlike 不- ('non-'), 未- implies work begun that has not yet reached its intended finish.

本.etymology: Read both as Sino-Japanese *hon* (from Middle Chinese 本 *pwonX*, 'root of a tree, base, origin, bound volume/book, counter for long cylindrical objects') and native Japanese *moto* ('base, origin').

history.meaning: tree root; foundation; original text; book
book; main/present; counter for long thin objects

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 本

本人.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 本人 (honnin), from Chinese 本人 ('the person himself/herself, the principal in question'), combining 本 ('original, principal, this') + 人 ('person').

history.meaning: the person himself/herself; the person in question

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 本人

本名.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 本名 (honmyō), combining 本 ('original, true, real') + 名 ('name'), contrasted with a stage name, pen name, or alias.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 本名

本当.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 本 ('root, origin, true') and 当 ('hit the mark, right, proper'). Historical dictionaries record 本当 in the sense of 'truth' in a 1770 work and 'a genuine or proper state' in a 1785 work; the shorter colloquial form ほんと arose by vowel shortening from ほんとう.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 本当

本当に.etymology: Adverbial form of the Sino-Japanese noun/na-adjective 本当 (hontō, 'truth, reality, genuineness', from 本 'true, original' + 当 'right, proper, hitting the mark') + particle に.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 本当

本当は.etymology: Discourse adverbial/conjunctive phrase formed from Sino-Japanese ほんとう (本当, 'truth, reality') + topic/contrastive particle は ('as for the truth -> in reality, actually').

history.meaning: actually; in fact; to tell the truth

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 本当

本棚.etymology: Hybrid compound combining Sino-Japanese ほん (本, 'book') + native Japanese だな (棚, rendaku form of たな 'shelf, rack').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 本棚

本物.etymology: Hybrid compound combining Sino-Japanese ほん (本, 'true, genuine, original') + native Japanese もの (物, 'thing, article').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 本物

札.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *puda* (札, 'wooden writing tablet, tag, placard, talisman'), undergoing medial *-p- > -f-* to *fuda*; also read Sino-Japanese *satsu* ('banknote, bill').

history.meaning: tag, label, card, talisman (fuda); paper bill/banknote (satsu)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 札

机.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tukuwe* (机・案, 'low table or stand for offerings, food, or books'), attested in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki; often analyzed as *tuki₂* ('vessel/stand') + *uwe* (居ゑ, 'setting down').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 机

杉.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sugi₁* (杉, 'Japanese cedar, *Cryptomeria japonica*'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; traditionally connected with すぐ (直ぐ, 'straight, upright') from its tall straight trunk.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 杉

条例.etymology: Sino-Japanese legal compound 条例 (jōrei), from Chinese 條例 ('itemized regulations, statutes, precedents'), combining 条 ('clause, article') + 例 ('rule, precedent'); in modern Japan, a municipal or prefectural ordinance.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 条例

来る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese irregular (k-irregular / ka-hen) verb *ku* (来, 'to come, approach the speaker's deictic center'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 来る

来年.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 来年 (rainen), from Classical Chinese 來年 ('the coming year, next year'), combining 来 ('come, next') + 年 ('year').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 来年

来月.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 来月 (raigetsu), combining 来 ('coming, next') + 月 ('month').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 来月

来週.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 来週 (raishū), combining 来 ('coming, next') + 週 ('week').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 来週

板.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ita* (板, 'wooden board, plank, flat metal sheet'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: board; plank; plate; cutting board; stage

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 板

枕.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *makura* (枕, 'pillow, headrest'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; widely analyzed as derived from まk- (巻く・纏く, 'to roll up, cushion the head') + suffix *-ra* (or くら 座 'seat/rest').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 枕

枕元.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining まくら (枕, 'pillow') + もと (元・下, 'base, vicinity, beside').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 枕元

枝.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *eda* (earlier also *ye*, 枝, 'tree branch, bough, twig'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 枝

柔らかい.etymology: Derived in Late Middle Japanese as an i-adjective from the classical naru-adjective やはらかなり (柔らかなり・軟らかなり, 'soft, pliant, gentle'), built on the root *yapa-* + suffixes *-ra-ka*.

history.form: やはらかなり (柔らかなり)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 柔らかい

案内.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 案内 (annai), originally a medieval Japanese administrative term ('the contents inside a written document or desk [案] -> prior knowledge of circumstances'), which developed into 'showing the way, guidance, invitation'.

history.meaning: contents of an official document; inside knowledge of a matter

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 案内

梁.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pari* (梁, 'horizontal roof beam spanning pillars'), likely derived from はる (張る, 'to stretch across, span').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 梁

棚.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tana* (棚, 'flat board or platform suspended horizontally, shelf, trellis'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; often analyzed as *ta-* ('hand') + *na*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 棚

森.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mo₂ri* (森・杜, 'sacred grove of trees around a shrine, dense woods'), attested in the Man'yōshū; cognate with もる (盛る, 'to heap up, rise thickly').

history.meaning: sacred shrine grove; thick stand of trees

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 森

椅子.etymology: Borrowed from Middle/Early Mandarin Chinese 椅子 ('chair'), combining 椅 ('chair, catalpa wood') and noun suffix 子, retaining the Tang-Song reading いす.

検査.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 検査 (kensa), from Chinese 檢査 ('to examine, inspect, verify'), combining 検 ('examine, check') + 査 ('investigate').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 検査

楽しみ.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of たのしむ (楽しむ, 'to enjoy, take pleasure in, look forward to').

history.meaning: enjoyment; pleasure; something looked forward to

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 楽しみ

楽しむ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tanosimu* / *tanosibu* (楽しむ・楽しぶ, 'to feel joy, take delight in'), derived from the adjective たのし (楽し, 'delightful, abundant, joyful') + verbalizer *-mu*.

history.form: たのしぶ / たのしむ (楽しむ)

history.meaning: enjoy; have fun; take pleasure in

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 楽しむ

楽譜.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 楽 ('music') and 譜 ('chronicle, systematic chart, notation'), denoting written musical notation or a score.

構う.etymology: Inherited from Classical Japanese lower bigrade verb *kamafu* (構ふ, 'to build, set up, prepare'), which shifted to a four-grade/godan verb in Late Middle Japanese with the senses 'to mind, care about, look after, tease, banish'.

history.meaning: pay heed to; mind; interfere with
mind; care about; look after; tease

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 構う

様子.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 様子 (yōsu), from Tang/Song vernacular Chinese 樣子 ('model, shape, appearance, air, state of affairs').

history.meaning: state of affairs; appearance; look; sign

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 様子

横.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *yo₂ko₂* (横, 'horizontal direction, side, width, crosswise'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 横

樫.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *kasi* (橿・樫, 'evergreen oak, *Quercus* subgenus *Cyclobalanopsis*'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, prized for its hard, dense timber (written with the kokuji 樫 from 木 'tree' + 堅 'hard').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 樫

橋.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pasi* (橋, 'bridge, stepping structure across a gap'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; cognate with 階 (*pasi*, 'stairs, ladder') and 間 (*pasi*, 'interval between two points').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 橋

機転.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 機転 (kiten), combining 機 ('pivotal moment, mental trigger, opportunity') + 転 ('turn, shift quickly'), denoting quick-wittedness or presence of mind.

history.meaning: quick mental adaptability to the moment

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 機転

機関車.etymology: Meiji-era Sino-Japanese compound 機関車 (kikansha), combining 機関 ('engine, mechanism, steam engine') + 車 ('wheeled vehicle, car'), coined to translate English *locomotive (engine)*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 機関車

欠けにくい.etymology: Compound adjective formed from the continuative stem かけ of かける (欠ける, 'to chip, break off') + auxiliary adjective -にくい (難い, 'hard to ..., resistant to ...').

history.form: 欠けにくい (かけにくい)
history.meaning: chip-resistant; hard to chip or break off

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 欠ける

欠ける.etymology: Intransitive ichidan verb *kakeru* ('to chip, break off at the edge, wane, be lacking'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade かく (欠く・闕く), the intransitive partner of godan 欠く.

history.meaning: chip away; wane (of the moon); be missing
be chipped; be missing; lack; wane

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 欠ける

次.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tugi₁* (次, 'next in order, succession, stage'), nominalized from the continuative stem of the verb つぐ (次ぐ・継ぐ, 'to follow directly after, succeed').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 次

歌.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *uta* (歌・唄, 'song, chant, Japanese waka poem'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; cognate with the verb うたふ (歌ふ, 'to sing, chant') and うったふ (訴ふ).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 歌

歌う.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *utapu* (歌ふ, 'to sing aloud, chant in rhythm, recite verse'), derived from うた (歌) + iterative/verbal suffix *-pu*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 歌う

止まる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese intransitive verb *to₂maru* (止まる・留まる・泊まる, 'to come to a halt, stop, remain, lodge'), paired with transitive とむ/とめる (止める).

history.form: とまる (止まる・留まる)

history.meaning: stop; halt; perch; be shut off

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 止まる

止める.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *tomeru* ('to stop, halt, fasten, turn off, dissuade'), continuing Old Japanese lower bigrade とむ (止む・留む).

history.meaning: bring to a halt; detain; fasten

history.form: 止める (とめる / やめる)
history.meaning: stop; halt; park; turn off (tomeru); quit, cancel (yameru)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 止める

正しい.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *tadasi* (正し, 'straight, upright, rightful, accurate, legitimate'), attested in the Man'yōshū; cognate with ただ (直, 'direct, straight') and ただす (正す).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 正しい

正午.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 正午 (shōgo), from Classical Chinese 正午 ('exact middle of the Hour of the Horse [11 a.m.–1 p.m.], high noon'), combining 正 ('exact') + 午 ('the seventh earthly branch, midday').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 正午

正式.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 正式 (seishiki), from Classical Chinese 正式 ('proper model, regular prescribed form'), combining 正 ('proper, orthodox, official') + 式 ('ceremony, form, standard').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 正式

正直.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 正直 (shōjiki), from Classical Chinese 正直 ('upright and straight, free from crookedness'), read with go-on *shōjiki* in everyday Japanese for 'honest, frank, candid'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 正直

正確.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 正確 (seikaku), combining 正 ('correct, right') + 確 ('firm, certain, exact').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 正確

正社員.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 正社員 (seishain), prefixing 正 ('regular, full, permanent') to 社員 ('company employee, staff member').

history.meaning: full-time permanent employee; regular staff member

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 正社員

歩く.etymology: Inherited from Late Old / Early Middle Japanese *aruku* (歩く, 'to walk, go about on foot'), a vowel-assimilated variant of Old Japanese *ariku* (歩く・ありく, 'to walk around, roam').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 歩く

歩ける.etymology: Potential ichidan form (*arukeru*, 'can walk, be able to walk') derived from the godan verb あるく (歩く, 'to walk').

history.meaning: be able to walk; can walk

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 歩く

歴史.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 歴史 (rekishi), from Chinese 歷史 ('successive records of past eras, history'), combining 歴 ('pass through in succession') + 史 ('chronicle, historian'); popularized in the Meiji era as the standard translation of Western *history*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 歴史

残す.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese transitive verb *no₂ko₂su* (残す・遺す, 'to leave behind, save, spare'), paired with intransitive のこる (残る).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 残す

残り.etymology: Deverbal noun from the continuative stem of のこる (残る, 'to remain, be left over').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 残り

残る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese intransitive verb *no₂ko₂ru* (残る, 'to remain behind, be left over, survive'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 残る

残念.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 残念 (zannen), combining 残 ('remain behind') + 念 ('thought, longing, regret'), originally 'lingering regret that remains in the heart' in medieval Japanese.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 残念

段.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 段 (dan), from Middle Chinese 段 (*dwanH*, 'section, piece, division, step/tier'), used in Japanese for steps of a staircase, tiers, stages, or ranks.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 段

段ボール箱.etymology: Modern compound combining 段ボール (danbōru, 'corrugated cardboard', coined in the Meiji era from 段 'stepped/fluted ridges' + ボール 'board', from English *cardboard*) + 箱 (hako, 'box').

history.form: 段ボール箱 (だんボールばこ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 段ボール

母.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *papa* (母, 'mother'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; medial *-p-* spirantized to *-f-* and *-w-* while initial *p-* became *f-* > *h-*, yielding *haha* (with dialectal/polite assimilation in some periods).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 母

母さん.etymology: Polite and affectionate kinship term combining かあ- (from an expressive lengthening inside おかあさん / かあさん, attested from late Edo speech) + honorific suffix -さん, written with 母 ('mother').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 母さん

毎年.etymology: Sino-Japanese / hybrid temporal noun read *maitoshi* (Sino-Japanese 毎 'every' + native とし 'year') or *mainen* (pure Sino-Japanese 毎年, from Classical Chinese 毎年 'every year').

history.form: 毎年 (まいとし / まいねん)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 毎年

毎日.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 毎日 (mainichi), from Classical Chinese 每日 ('every day'), combining 毎 ('each, every') + 日 ('day').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 毎日

毎朝.etymology: Hybrid compound *maiasa* combining Sino-Japanese prefix 毎 (mai-, 'every') + native Japanese あさ (朝, 'morning').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 毎朝

毎週.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 毎週 (maishū), combining 毎 ('every, each') + 週 ('week').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 毎週

比べる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *kurabu* (比ぶ・較ぶ, 'to place side by side to measure or contest, compare'), derived from くら (座・位, 'seat, rank, position').

history.meaning: match side by side; compare; contest

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 比べる

毛布.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 毛布 (mōfu), from Chinese 毛布 ('woolen cloth'), combining 毛 ('wool, hair') + 布 ('cloth'); adopted in Meiji Japan (initially also read *ketto* from English *blanket*) as *mōfu* for a woolen blanket.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 毛布

気.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 気 (ki / ke), from Middle Chinese 氣 (*kʰjɨjH*, 'vapor, breath, vital energy, spirit, mood, disposition'), deeply integrated into Japanese idiom for mind, attention, and atmosphere.

history.meaning: spirit; mind; heart; mood; attention; air/sign

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気

気づく.etymology: Compound godan verb *kizuku* (気づく・気付く), grammaticalized from the clause 気がつく ('one's attention/mind attaches to something -> to notice, realize, regain consciousness').

history.form: きがつく / きづく (気付く)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気付く

気に入る.etymology: Idiomatic phrasal verb 気に入る (ki ni iru, 'to enter into one's spirit/fancy'), attested from late medieval and Edo Japanese for 'to be pleased with, like, take a liking to'.

history.meaning: suit one's mind or taste; be pleasing
like; be pleased with; take a fancy to

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気に入る

気の毒.etymology: Nominal/na-adjectival phrase 気の毒 (ki no doku), literally 'poison to the spirit'. In Edo-period usage it first meant 'troublesome or regrettable to one's own mind', and subsequently shifted to 'pitiful, unfortunate, feeling sorry for someone else'.

history.meaning: pitiful; unfortunate; sorry to trouble you

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気の毒

気分.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 気分 (kibun), combining 気 ('vital spirit, mood, humor') + 分 ('state, condition, lot'), denoting one's physical or emotional mood and state of feeling.

history.meaning: state of health or humor; mood
feeling; mood; state of health; atmosphere

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気分

気持ち.etymology: Hybrid compound combining Sino-Japanese き (気, 'mind, spirit, mood') + native Japanese もち (持ち, from 持つ 'holding, maintaining').

history.meaning: way of holding one's mind; frame of mind; sensation

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気持ち

気持ちよい.etymology: Compound adjective combining きもち (気持ち, 'feeling, sensation') + よい (良い, 'good, pleasant'), meaning 'pleasant, comfortable, refreshing'.

history.form: 気持ちよい / 気持ち良い (きもちよい)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気持ち良い

気軽.etymology: Hybrid na-adjective combining Sino-Japanese き (気, 'spirit, mind, mood') + native Japanese がる (軽, rendaku form of the stem かる- of 軽い 'light').

history.meaning: lighthearted; casual; free and easy; unhesitating

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 気軽

水.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *mi₁du* (水, combining form *mi₁-*, 'water, fresh cold water'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; also read Sino-Japanese *sui* (from Middle Chinese 水 *sywijX*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 水

水性.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 水性 (suisei), combining 水 ('water') + 性 ('nature, property'), referring in modern usage especially to water-based paints, inks, or adhesives.

history.meaning: the nature of water; aquatic nature

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 水性

水曜.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 水曜 (suiyō), literally 'luminary of Mercury (the Water Star, 水星)' from the classical seven-planet astrological cycle, serving as the short form of 水曜日 ('Wednesday').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 水曜

水曜日.etymology: Compound of 水曜 ('Mercury day', linked to the Five Phases element 水 'water') and 日 ('day') in the seven-day week.

水漏れ.etymology: Hybrid/native compound combining みず (水, 'water') + もれ (漏れ, continuative stem of 漏れる 'to leak').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 水漏れ

水道管.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 水道管 (suidōkan), combining 水道 ('waterworks, water supply conduit', from 水 'water' + 道 'channel/way') + 管 ('pipe, tube').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 水道管

氷.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ko₂pori* (氷, 'ice'), nominalized from the continuative stem of the Old Japanese verb *ko₂poru* (氷る・凍る, 'to freeze, congeal'); underwent medial *-p- > -f- > -w- > Ø* to modern *kōri*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 氷

決定.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 決定 (kettei), from Classical and Buddhist Chinese 決定 ('to settle decisively, fix without doubt'), combining 決 ('breach a dike, decide, resolve') + 定 ('fix, settle').

history.form: けつぢゃう / けってい (決定)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 決定

汽車.etymology: Late Edo / Meiji-era Sino-Japanese compound 汽車 (kisha), combining 汽 ('steam, vapor', short for 蒸気 *jōki*) + 車 ('wheeled vehicle, carriage'), coined for a steam train.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 汽車

油.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *abura* (油・脂, 'oil, fat, grease, tallow'), attested in the Nihon Shoki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 油

油断.etymology: Sino-Japanese / Buddhist compound 油断 (yudan), literally 'cutting off the flow of oil'. Derived from a parable in the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra* (涅槃経) in which a man ordered to carry a bowl brimful of oil without spilling a single drop on pain of death must never relax his attention; hence 'momentary lapse of attention, carelessness, negligence'.

history.meaning: letting one's guard or attention lapse
negligence; carelessness; inattention; being off one's guard

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 油断

沿う.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese intransitive verb *so₂pu* (添ふ・沿ふ, 'to accompany closely, run alongside, conform to'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; spelled 沿う specifically when following a line, river, road, or policy.

history.meaning: run along; follow (a river, road, or plan); meet (expectations)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 沿う

泊まる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese intransitive verb *to₂maru* (泊まる・止まる・留まる, 'to stop, come to rest, anchor in a harbor, stay overnight'), specialized in orthography as 泊まる for anchoring a boat or lodging for the night.

history.meaning: moor a boat for the night; lodge overnight

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 泊まる

法律.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 法律 (hōritsu), from Classical Chinese 法律 ('laws and statutes'), combining 法 ('law, norm, model') + 律 ('penal statute, code'); adopted in the Meiji era as the standard term for statutory law.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 法律

泡.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *awa* (泡・沫, 'foam, bubble, froth on water'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 泡

泡立てる.etymology: Compound ichidan verb combining あわ (泡, 'foam, bubbles') + たてる (立てる, 'to raise, whip up').

history.form: あわだつ / あわだてる (泡立てる)
history.meaning: work into a foam; whip up lather

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 泡立てる

泣く.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *naku* (泣く・鳴く, 'to cry out, weep, sing/call of birds and animals'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; written 泣く for human weeping and 鳴く for animal/bird cries.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 泣く

注ぎ口.etymology: Native Japanese compound combining そそぎ (注ぎ, continuative stem of 注ぐ 'to pour') + ぐち (口, rendaku form of くち 'mouth, opening, spout').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 注ぎ口

注ぐ.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *so₂so₂ku* > *sosogu* (注ぐ・灌ぐ, 'to pour liquid into, flow into, sprinkle, devote oneself to') and *tsugu* (注ぐ・継ぐ, 'to pour into a cup or vessel').

history.form: そそく / そそぐ (注ぐ)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 注ぐ

注文.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound of 注 ('pour, fix attention, annotate') and 文 ('writing, document'), which shifted in medieval/early-modern Japanese commerce from 'an itemized written list' to 'placing an order for goods'.

洋風.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 洋風 (yōfū), combining 洋 ('Western, overseas', short for 西洋 *seiyō*) + 風 ('style, manner'), contrasted with 和風 (wafū, 'Japanese style').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 洋風

洗う.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *arapu* (洗ふ, 'to wash with water, cleanse, rinse, investigate'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 洗う

洗面所.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 洗面所 (senmenjo), combining 洗面 ('washing the face', from 洗 'wash' + 面 'face') + 所 ('place, room').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 洗面所

流す.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese transitive verb *nagasu* (流す, 'to let flow, set adrift, wash away, exile'), paired with intransitive ながる/ながれる (流れる).

history.meaning: set afloat on a current; wash away; banish
let flow; drain; flush; broadcast/play (music); shed (tears/sweat)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 流す

流れる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *nagaru* (流る, 'to flow, stream, drift along, pass by'), becoming modern ichidan *nagareru*.

history.meaning: flow; stream; drift; be washed away; be called off

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 流れる

海塩.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 海塩 (かいえん), from 海 ('sea, ocean') and 塩 ('salt').
海塩.notes: Distinguishes evaporated sea salt from rock salt (岩塩 がんえん).

浸す.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese transitive verb *pitasu* (浸す・漬す, 'to soak, steep, dip in liquid'), paired with intransitive ひたる (浸る, 'to be immersed in').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 浸す

消える.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *ki₁yu* (消ゆ, 'to melt away, go out, vanish, disappear'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, becoming modern ichidan *kieru*.

history.meaning: melt (of snow/dew); go out (of fire); vanish
go out; disappear; vanish; fade away

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 消える

深い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pukasi* (深し, 'deep, profound, dense, late in a season or night'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: deep; profound; thick (of fog/woods); close (of a relationship)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 深い

深呼吸.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 深呼吸 (shinkokyū), prefixing 深 ('deep') to 呼吸 ('breathing, respiration', from 呼 'exhale' + 吸 'inhale').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 深呼吸

混ぜる.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *mazeru* ('to mix, blend, stir together'), continuing Classical Japanese lower bigrade まず (混ず・交ず), paired with intransitive まじる/まざる (混じる・混ざる).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 混ぜる

混む.etymology: Inherited from Classical and Late Middle Japanese *komu* (込む・混む, 'to crowd in, be packed together'), specialized in modern orthography as 混む when referring to crowds or traffic congestion.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 混む

清潔.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 清潔 (seiketsu), from Classical Chinese 清潔 ('clear and pure, uncorrupted, clean'), combining 清 ('clear, pure') + 潔 ('clean, spotless').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 清潔

済ませる.etymology: Transitive ichidan verb *sumaseru* ('to finish, get through with, settle, make do with'), originally the causative form of すむ (済む, 'to come to an end, be settled'), alongside godan 済ます.

history.form: すませる / すます (済ませる)
history.meaning: bring to completion; settle; make do
finish; get done; settle; make do with

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 済ませる

済む.etymology: Etymologically the same native Japanese verb as すむ (澄む, 'to become clear, settle' of muddy water). In Early Modern merchant and everyday usage, 'for things to settle down without trouble' developed the sense 'to be settled (of an account or business), be finished, be over', written with 済.

history.meaning: be settled (of debts or affairs); come to a close
end; be completed; be settled; be excusable

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 済む

渡す.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese transitive verb *watasu* (渡す, 'to carry across water, bridge across, hand over'), paired with intransitive わたる (渡る).

history.meaning: ferry across; span across; hand over
hand over; deliver; ferry across; lay across

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 渡す

渡せる.etymology: Potential ichidan form (*wataseru*, 'can hand over, be able to pass/deliver') derived from the godan verb わたす (渡す, 'to hand over, pass across').

history.meaning: be able to hand over; can give/deliver

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 渡す

渡る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese intransitive verb *wataru* (渡る・亘る, 'to cross over water or a bridge, pass across, extend throughout'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: cross over (a river, sea, or sky); pass through
cross (a bridge, street, or river); migrate; be handed over

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 渡る

温かい.etymology: Same native Japanese word *atatakai* as 暖かい (from classical あたたかなり 'warm, mild'), conventionally written 温かい when referring to warm food, liquids, touch, or human kindness.

history.form: あたたかなり (温かなり)

history.meaning: warm (to the touch, of food/drink, or of heart/reception)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 温かい

測る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pakaru* (測る・量る・計る・図る, 'to reckon, measure, weigh, fathom, plan'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; spelled 測る specifically for measuring depth, length, area, or physical quantities.

history.form: はかる (測る・量る・計る)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 測る

湯呑み.etymology: Native Japanese compound 湯呑み / 湯飲み (yunomi), from ゆ (湯, 'hot water, hot tea') + のみ (飲み, continuative stem of 飲む 'to drink'), referring to a cylindrical handleless ceramic teacup.

history.form: ゆのみ (湯飲み・湯呑み)
history.meaning: cup for drinking hot water or tea

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 湯呑み

湿る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sime₂ru* (湿る, 'to become damp, moisten, be subdued or quiet'), attested in the Man'yōshū; paired with transitive しめす (湿す).

history.meaning: absorb moisture; become damp; grow quiet
become damp; get moist; be dampened

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 湿る

湿気.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 湿気 (colloquially read しっけ with gemination, alongside しっき), from 湿 ('damp, moist') and 気 ('air, vapour').
湿気.notes: Central everyday word during Japan's rainy season when wooden doors and piano actions absorb moisture.

満室.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 満室 (manshitsu), combining 満 ('full') + 室 ('room'), indicating that a hotel, inn, or building has no vacancies.

history.meaning: no vacancy; fully booked (of rooms); full room

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 満室

満杯.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 満杯 (manpai), combining 満 ('full') + 杯 ('cup, vessel, capacity'), literally 'a full cup' and by extension 'filled to capacity, chock-full'.

history.meaning: a cup filled to the brim

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 満杯

満点.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 満点 (manten), combining 満 ('full, complete') + 点 ('point, mark, score'), meaning a perfect score or full marks.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 満点

準備.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 準備 (junbi), from Chinese 準備 ('to prepare beforehand, make ready in advance'), combining 準 ('level, standard, prepare') + 備 ('provide, equip, get ready').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 準備

滑る.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sube₂ru* (滑る・辷る, 'to slide smoothly, slip, glide'), attested in the Kojiki and Wamyō Ruijushō; cognate with すべすべ ('smooth').

history.meaning: glide; slip smoothly; step down from the throne
slip; slide; glide; skate/ski; fall flat (of a joke)

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 滑る

澄む.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *sumu* (澄む・清む, 'to become clear, transparent, untroubled, or pure' of water, sky, sound, or mind), attested in the Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: become clear and limpid (of water, moon, or sound)
become clear; be transparent; be serene

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 澄む

激しい.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pagesi* (激し・烈し, 'fierce, violent, tempestuous, intense'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

history.meaning: fierce (of wind or current); violent; intense

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 激しい

濃い.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *ko₂si* (濃し, 'deep in color, thick in consistency, strong in flavor'), attested in the Man'yōshū.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 濃い

濡らす.etymology: Transitive godan verb *nurasu* ('to wet, moisten, drench'), paired with intransitive ぬる/ぬれる (濡れる).

history.meaning: make wet; dampen with water, dew, or tears

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 濡らす

濡れる.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese lower bigrade verb *nuru* (濡る, 'to get wet, become damp'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū, becoming modern ichidan *nureru*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 濡れる

火.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *pi₂* (combining form *po₂-*, 'fire, flame'), attested in the Kojiki and Man'yōshū; also read Sino-Japanese *ka* (from Middle Chinese 火 *xwaX*).

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 火

火曜日.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 火曜日 (kayōbi), combining 火曜 ('Day of Mars, the Fire Star 火星' in the classical seven-luminary astrological cycle) + 日 ('day').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 火曜日

灰色.etymology: Compound combining native Japanese はい (灰, from Old Japanese *papi* 'ash') + いろ (色, 'color'), literally 'ash color'.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 灰色

炎.etymology: Inherited from Old Japanese *po₂-no-po* (火の穂, literally 'ear/spike of fire', comparing a leaping tongue of flame to an ear of grain *po*), which contracted via *ponopo > fonofo > honoo*.

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 炎

炭酸水.etymology: Modern Sino-Japanese scientific and culinary compound 炭酸水 (tansansui), combining 炭酸 ('carbonic acid, carbonation', coined in the late Edo/Rangaku period from 炭 'carbon' + 酸 'acid') + 水 ('water').

history.meaning: carbonated water; sparkling water; soda water

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 炭酸水

点.etymology: Sino-Japanese noun 点 (ten), from Middle Chinese 點 (*temX*, 'small black fleck, dot, speck, mark, point, to light/drip').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 点

点数.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 点数 (tensū), combining 点 ('point, mark, item') + 数 ('number, count'), denoting either a numerical score/grade or the number of items.

history.meaning: count of items; number of points
score; points; marks; number of items

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 点数

無事.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 無事 (buji), from Classical Chinese 無事 ('without incident, free from trouble or warfare, at peace'), combining 無 ('without') + 事 ('untoward incident, affair').

history.meaning: free of trouble or military incident; peaceful
safe; without incident; safe and sound

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 無事

無塗装.etymology: Sino-Japanese compound 無塗装 (mutosō), prefixing privative 無 ('un-, without') to 塗装 ('painting, coating, finish', from 塗 'paint/coat' + 装 'finish/dress').

sources.title: Shogakukan: Digital Daijisen / Selected Nihon Kokugo Daijiten — 塗装
